An Israeli soldier stands guard as young men gathered during a demonstration by Ultra-Orthodox Jews against Israel's military draft on June 17, 2026 outside the Beit Lid military base in Kfar Yona, Israel. Photo by Amir Levy/Getty Images.
_This article is being co-published with[Capital & Empire](https://substack.com/redirect/4eac0bcd-688c-400d-b42d-1323b7176dbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
Israel is at risk of civil war or state collapse, a classified CIA assessment warns, as years of genocide in Gaza and war in Lebanon and Iran deepen political, economic, and social fractures within the country.
The August report, titled "Fracture From Within," was compiled by experts in the CIA's Red Cell, according to two U.S. sources who described the contents of the report to Drop Site News. The Red Cell, which is the unit responsible for providing "alternative analysis" within the agency, produced the assessment through a combination of open source information and U.S. intelligence. The CIA did not respond to a request for comment.
CIA experts pointed to a volatile mix of pressures converging ahead of Israel's elections on October 27: economic crisis and soaring military spending; heavily armed veterans returning from prolonged combat, many carrying serious psychological trauma; growing fury over ultra-Orthodox men who are exempt from military service; escalating settler violence in the occupied West Bank; and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fighting to hold onto power and igniting a constitutional crisis.
The CIA's "red teams" are tasked with developing analysis and ideas that challenge prevailing assumptions and expose groupthink or blind spots that can take hold within the intelligence apparatus. "The writers of this are Israel experts," a source in the intelligence community noted, "this isn't a fantastical what if--with the upcoming election and the fissures in Israel we should take seriously their conclusion that Israel is one spark away from real internal conflict."
One of the deepest fractures in Israeli politics has emerged not over opposition to the country's war crimes--but over who is expected to fight and who is exempt. Ultra-Orthodox men have historically received broad exemptions from military service while continuing to receive state benefits, an arrangement that has become increasingly contentious amid repeated reserve mobilizations. Their collective refusal to serve is not rooted in opposition to Israel's wars, as ultra-Orthodox leaders argue that military service threatens religious life and their obligation to Torah study. But after years in which reservists have been repeatedly called away from their jobs and families, the [exemption](https://substack.com/redirect/6eee9751-81ad-463e-a025-4b2b0b394af1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has become a potent source of resentment in Israeli society. Households have also been absorbing the costs of Israel's belligerent policies. Food prices have reached [record highs](https://substack.com/redirect/d42a7a29-31de-479d-a3ad-eb044195be9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with the cost of food--including fresh fruit and vegetables--rising 9.5 percent over the past two years, deepening an already severe cost-of-living crisis after years of war.
Yet much of the opposition to Netanyahu is not opposition to Israel's brutality against Palestinians, but anger over how he has managed it. The major anti-Netanyahu Zionist parties are themselves divided over leadership and coalition strategy, while a central line of attack against Netanyahu has been his responsibility for the October 7 security failure. Recent [polling](https://substack.com/redirect/65ab0749-79ad-4362-94d4-b8a597c1a0fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has shown both the Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs struggling to reach the 61 seats required to govern.
The sources warned that the combination of political fracture and a growing population of heavily armed, traumatized veterans has historical precedents. "Famously the Freikorps of Germany were PTSD-addled veterans with weapons and bloodthirst," he said. "I'm not saying Israel post Gaza is Germany post-WWI but there are certainly aspects of this that ring similar to me."
Israel is also confronting growing isolation abroad, including an erosion of support in the United States that Israeli officials themselves have privately treated as a long-term threat. The August report pointed to Israel increasingly becoming a pariah state as a factor that could lead to state breakdown.
According to another CIA assessment Capital & Empire [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/0a4e3db7-1851-4345-b2c3-37acd68f6bda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in July, Israeli officials believe the American political consensus underpinning the alliance is breaking down and that continued reliance on billions of dollars in direct U.S. military aid may eventually become politically untenable. Their response has been to seek deeper integration into the American military, intelligence, and defense establishment--ties that would be harder for future governments to unwind. By this spring, 60% of Americans viewed Israel unfavorably, up from 53% a year earlier, according to a Pew Research Center [survey](https://substack.com/redirect/13af2ebb-7554-4c5b-89c8-9e0071abbeeb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
That deterioration of support is increasingly visible inside the U.S. national security establishment, as well. "The intelligence community, like America, like the military, like everywhere, is growing frustrated with the real and political capital that's spent on propping up Israel," the source said. "As we're moving forward with further integrating our military-industrial capacity with them, there's deep frustration that we're doing this for a country that dragged us into a war we're losing, a country that spies on us."
The CIA report also tried to game out how these pressures could interact if Israel's internal crisis deepened--how a single spark could turn political fracture into open civil conflict, and what would follow from there. Among the scenarios raised were foreign technology and artificial-intelligence companies pulling investment or personnel from Israel, further eroding an already strained economy, regional governments reconsidering the political and strategic value of deeper normalizing relations with Israel, and Hamas or Hezbollah exploiting a period of domestic weakness. The report specifically used the term "civil conflict," according to the sources.
For decades, Israel's power depended not only on weapons and American backing, but on the projection that its military dominance, intelligence superiority, and internal cohesion made the state effectively unbreakable. But as the assessment warned, beneath that projection of overwhelming force, Israel is accumulating economic, political, and social contradictions that military might alone may not be able to contain.

#

**Politico: Supreme Court to decide on right to own assault weapons**
**[Please rush a donation to GIFFORDS PAC >>**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261005-1-b&t=1&akid=11896%2E3935704%2EXVnlAZ)

Team —
In a few weeks, the Supreme Court will begin oral arguments to hear two cases on the constitutionality of assault weapons bans — likely deciding if weapons of war are allowed on our streets.
This is a big deal. Here’s what you need to know:
In 2012, our country experienced one of the deadliest school shootings in U.S. history. A gunman entered Sandy Hook Elementary School and used his semi-automatic rifle to fire off 154 bullets in less than five minutes. Twenty first-graders and six educators were killed.
Enough was enough. Connecticut lawmakers took action to ban dangerous weapons like AR-15’s in their state. Nine other states and D.C. followed suit, banning assault weapons. This was a massive win for public safety.
**The gun lobby wants to get rid of those bans.** If the gun lobby gets their wish, we could see even more weapons of war flooded into our neighborhoods — and there’s nothing your state or local government could do to stop it.
GIFFORDS is doing everything we can to save lives and elect leaders who care more about public safety than the gun lobby’s profits, but we can’t do it without you. So before arguments begin in the Supreme Court, we are asking:
**[Will you please rush an emergency contribution to power our work at GIFFORDS PAC today? We need a surge in donations to show the gun lobby that we are ready to end gun violence in America.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261005-1-b&t=3&akid=11896%2E3935704%2EXVnlAZ)

What's up, Angry Democrats? Matt here.
Everybody keeps talking about a blue wave. But what would a blue wave actually mean, and what could Democrats realistically do if they won control of both the House and Senate?
For this discussion, I am not going to complicate things with every possible outcome. I am not talking about Democrats winning the House while Republicans keep the Senate. I am also not talking about some massive Democratic supermajority that fundamentally changes the rules.
I am talking about the simplest realistic scenario: Democrats win a narrow majority in the House and at least 51 seats in the Senate.
What happens then?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e54ae6a-9fa5-48f5-8f4f-497d5d04f9eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
## **First, a Reality Check**
Winning Congress would not mean Democrats could suddenly pass anything they wanted.
Most legislation can still be blocked by the Senate filibuster unless Democrats have 60 votes, use budget reconciliation or change Senate rules. Even if a bill passes both chambers, it would still go to Donald Trump's desk. He could veto it, and overriding that veto would require two-thirds of both the House and Senate.
So let's be honest about what a narrow Democratic majority would mean.
It would be much better at stopping Trump, investigating Trump and slowing down the administration than passing an enormous Democratic legislative agenda.
* * *
## **1\. Block Trump 's Legislative Agenda**
Right now, Republicans control the House, Senate and executive branch. That gives Trump considerable freedom to move legislation through Congress when Republicans remain united.
If Democrats control both chambers, that stops.
Whether Trump wants another artificial-intelligence bill, another round of tax cuts, another funding package or those $5,000 bribery checks, Democrats would control whether that legislation receives a vote and what ultimately reaches his desk.
The same would apply to legislation involving immigration, energy, healthcare, military funding and the federal budget.
Trump could no longer expect Congress to rubber-stamp everything he wants...

| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/xQn8Lj2wKkc?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

Not $100. Not $50. Not even $25!

Just $15.

Friend, it's Michele Tafoya. I'm sure you've received plenty of political messages this time of year from thankless politicians who have spent the majority of their careers in Washington, lining their own pockets.To be candid with you, that's everything I'm NOT.
I spent the better part of my life on the sidelines watching the best athletes in the world compete at the highest level.
I know what it takes to be a winner, I've seen it firsthand.That's the pedigree I've brought to this campaign.
Not cutting corners, not cheating myself, or letting my team down.
But I can't be the only one bought in if we're going to succeed this fall, Friend.

It's going to take a group of us going the extra mile to create change.

Folks, I'm reaching out with an urgent request.
Adam Hamilton is the Democrat running for U.S. Senate in Kansas, and three polls in a row show him narrowly leading his Republican opponent. We can flip this seat blue.
**That 's why the GOP is panicking. Their top super PAC just launched a MASSIVE ad buy in Kansas to turn the tides against Adam and boost his opponent - and he needs our immediate grassroots support to fight back.**
You've stood by my side while I've faced these kinds of attacks. Now, I'm asking you to show up for Adam. [Will you make a split donation of $10 between my campaign and Adam Hamilton's right now? Flipping this seat - and the Senate - is crucial to getting our country back on the right track.](https://substack.com/redirect/2387658c-8566-40bf-9744-5c65634163d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Adam has been a pastor for the past 36 years, and he's a fifth-generation Kansan.
He's been called to run for Senate for many of the same reasons I have: He loves his home state. He cares deeply about the future of our country. He knows that Washington DC's chaos and corruption are making life harder for folks, and he's ready to fix things.
With experts at RealClearPolitics calling this race a "Toss Up" and the polls continuing to shift in his direction, Adam has what it takes to flip Kansas for the first time in nearly a _century_.
But not without your support - right here, right now. He's getting outspent by the GOP, and he simply cannot fight back without you.**[Will you split $10 to help Adam and me flip our respective seats this November and build a brighter future for all?](https://substack.com/redirect/2387658c-8566-40bf-9744-5c65634163d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you.
Roy Cooper

House Minority Leader Jim Durkin wears a mask during the legislative session. (Credit: Justin L. Fowler of The State Journal-Register)
By Jacqueline Garretson, Opinion Contributor

It has been more than five years since COVID-19 changed our lives, but for many Illinois families, the consequences never really went away. Businesses were lost, jobs disappeared, families drained their savings, and children lost something that can never be replaced: their childhood.

Under Gov. JB Pritzker, Illinois families spent 1,155 days under some form of COVID-era emergency declarations, restrictions, and executive orders. For more than three years, Illinoisans lived with a government response that repeatedly changed how we worked, learned, worshiped, and interacted with one another. What was initially presented as a temporary emergency became a prolonged period of government intervention that affected every aspect of daily life.

But the people who paid the greatest price were often those with the least ability to understand what was happening: our children.

In a matter of weeks, their entire world changed. Schools closed. Sports disappeared. Friends became faces on computer screens. Birthday parties, school activities, graduations, and family gatherings were canceled.

Children were isolated during some of the most important developmental years of their lives, and many are still dealing with the consequences. Parents watched their children struggle with anxiety, fear, isolation, and academic setbacks. Years later, many students remain behind where they should be.

Yet instead of confronting those failures honestly, Illinois continues to lower the bar and declare victory.

Changing standards doesn’t change reality. If students are struggling academically, lowering expectations doesn’t make them more successful. It simply makes the numbers look better. Parents in Illinois deserve an education system that tells the truth about where our children are; not one that manipulates the measurements to make politicians look more successful.

And here’s the part voters should not forget: Democrats weren’t the only politicians who supported the COVID response. Some Republicans did too.

Former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin, along with others in the party, supported restrictions, defended the status quo, and failed to challenge the system, while families and businesses were suffering. Politicians shouldn’t be more concerned with maintaining political relationships than standing up for the people who elected them.

Today, former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin has endorsed JB Pritzker for Governor. Durkin’s endorsement is a political nod of approval to the very Governor whose COVID policies left such a lasting mark on Illinois families.

To me, that endorsement says a lot. It is a reminder that the old political establishment has never been as divided as the party labels would have us believe.

There was, however, a Republican who was willing to challenge the governor when it mattered: Darren Bailey.

I watched Darren stand on the House floor and tell the political establishment that the path Illinois was taking was wrong. He challenged Pritzker’s restrictions. And while others were willing to go along to get along, Darren was willing to stand up and fight.

You don’t have to agree with Darren Bailey on every issue to recognize the importance of political courage.

Leadership isn’t simply agreeing with the majority when it is politically convenient. Sometimes leadership means standing alone and telling the people in power that they have gone too far.

The next crisis will eventually come. When it does, Illinois families need leaders who understand that government power must have limits and that emergency authority cannot become a blank check.

We need leaders who will listen to parents, protect children, support small businesses, and question the establishment when its power becomes unchecked.

Because those 1,155 days weren’t just numbers on a calendar. They represented birthdays that couldn’t be celebrated, seasons that couldn’t be played, businesses that never reopened, jobs that disappeared, and children who lost years they will never get back.

Five years later, Illinois families are still picking up the pieces. They don’t need politicians to tell them everything worked. They know it didn’t.

They deserve the truth. They deserve accountability. And they deserve leaders who will put people before politics.

That leader is Darren Bailey.

(Credit: Justin L. Fowler of The State Journal-Register) By Jacqueline Garretson, Opinion Contributor It has been more than five years since COVID-19 changed our lives, but for many Illinois families, the consequences never really went away. Businesses were lost, jobs disappeared, families drained their savings, and children lost something that can never be replaced: their childhood. Under Gov. JB Pritzker, Illinois families spent 1,155 days under some form of COVID-era emergency declarations, restrictions, and executive orders. For more than three years, Illinoisans lived with a government response that repeatedly changed how we worked, learned, worshiped, and interacted with one another. What was initially presented as a temporary emergency became a prolonged period of government intervention that affected every aspect of daily life. But the people who paid the greatest price were often those with the least ability to understand what was happening: our children. In a matter of weeks, their entire world changed. Schools closed. Sports disappeared. Friends became faces on computer screens. Birthday parties, school activities, graduations, and family gatherings were canceled. Children were isolated during some of the most important developmental years of their lives, and many are still dealing with the consequences. Parents watched their children struggle with anxiety, fear, isolation, and academic setbacks. Years later, many students remain behind where they should be. Yet instead of confronting those failures honestly, Illinois continues to lower the bar and declare victory. Changing standards doesn’t change reality. If students are struggling academically, lowering expectations doesn’t make them more successful. It simply makes the numbers look better. Parents in Illinois deserve an education system that tells the truth about where our children are; not one that manipulates the measurements to make politicians look more successful. And here’s the part voters should not forget: Democrats weren’t the only politicians who supported the COVID response. Some Republicans did too. Former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin, along with others in the party, supported restrictions, defended the status quo, and failed to challenge the system, while families and businesses were suffering. Politicians shouldn’t be more concerned with maintaining political relationships than standing up for the people who elected them. Today, former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin has endorsed JB Pritzker for Governor. Durkin’s endorsement is a political nod of approval to the very Governor whose COVID policies left such a lasting mark on Illinois families. To me, that endorsement says a lot. It is a reminder that the old political establishment has never been as divided as the party labels would have us believe. There was, however, a Republican who was willing to challenge the governor when it mattered: Darren Bailey. I watched Darren stand on the House floor and tell the political establishment that the path Illinois was taking was wrong. He challenged Pritzker’s restrictions. And while others were willing to go along to get along, Darren was willing to stand up and fight. You don’t have to agree with Darren Bailey on every issue to recognize the importance of political courage. Leadership isn’t simply agreeing with the majority when it is politically convenient. Sometimes leadership means standing alone and telling the people in power that they have gone too far. The next crisis will eventually come. When it does, Illinois families need leaders who understand that government power must have limits and that emergency authority cannot become a blank check. We need leaders who will listen to parents, protect children, support small businesses, and question the establishment when its power becomes unchecked. Because those 1,155 days weren’t just numbers on a calendar. They represented birthdays that couldn’t be celebrated, seasons that couldn’t be played, businesses that never reopened, jobs that disappeared, and children who lost years they will never get back. Five years later, Illinois families are still picking up the pieces. They don’t need politicians to tell them everything worked. They know it didn’t. They deserve the truth. They deserve accountability. And they deserve leaders who will put people before politics. That leader is Darren Bailey. clean_body: | | | | Friend, So I've stopped trying to read the tea leaves, and I'm just going to keep working to save this country from the people who would guarantee two years of investigations, impeachments, and decay. If the Democrats get back power, they won't spend the next two years securing the border, bringing down prices, or doing anything that makes your life better. They've already made clear that their plan is endless hearings, subpoenas, and impeachment theater built to grind this country to a halt. That's why I'm coming to you today, Friend, and asking you to go on the record before the Midterms. | Elections are determined by turnout, not by polls. I remember when the liberal Detroit newspaper had Republican candidate John Engler 9 points behind the incumbent Democrat governor on a Saturday. I don’t think that many people changed their minds. I think the liberal poll was designed to demoralize Republicans and keep them home. You're going to see a lot of polls like that between now and November, Friend, and every one of them will be built to convince you that the race is already over, that your vote doesn't matter, and that you might as well stay home. Don't believe them for a second. Sincerely, Newt Gingrich Former Speaker of the House | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee.

**I’m not some cookie-cutter politician.**
I used to work as a scientist — a geologist, to be specific. After our company was sold and I got laid off, I organized and opened Colorado’s first brewpub, helping revitalize LoDo, a neglected warehouse district in Denver.
I never imagined I’d run for office. I wandered into public service because I felt like our elected officials were mainly making decisions to get re-elected, not solve problems for their constituents. So I ran for mayor, then governor, and eventually senator.
Even though my commute to work got a whole lot longer, my focus hasn’t changed. I’m still deadset on **putting Colorado families first and getting stuff done. And that’s exactly what we’ve done!**
As Denver’s Mayor, we unified the metro area to expand and rejuvenate our public transit. As Governor, we took Colorado from 40th in job creation to the #1 economy in the nation for three straight years. And as your senator, we wrote and passed the largest-ever effort to fight climate change, passed the most consequential housing bill in decades, and lowered drug costs for seniors.
Now I’m running for reelection to finish what we’ve started. We need to help Democrats take back the Senate and bring MAGA’s ruthless agenda to a halt. And we need you on our side.
Unlike other politicians, we don’t take money from corporate PACs. Instead, we rely on grassroots folks like you.
[That’s why I'm depending on your contribution today to help us defend Colorado. Even just $5 here or $10 there goes a long way in a campaign like ours. So we have to ask: will you chip in whatever is meaningful to you today? Together, we can defend this must-hold seat and put power back in the hands of working people:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140726281/651344984/1681514997?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_100526_bio&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlYWE0ZmM0ZC1lMGMwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wJuKFGjCDPekr6qHJFnFRegMnerSXl40GPZzaU8C7d8=)

Last week, a reporter asked me a question I haven't been able to shake.
If Democrats win back the House and the Senate, should they investigate every member of Donald Trump's family? Even Melania? Even Barron?
I could hear what was underneath it. Surely some of them should be off-limits. Surely there's a line. It's the political version of "women and children first" on the Titanic, as if the lifeboats were reserved for the people we feel a little squeamish about scrutinizing.
My answer took about half a second: _Absolutely_. Investigate Melania Trump. Investigate Barron Trump. Investigate all of them.
There are no sacred cows when it comes to the most corrupt family in American history. They have stolen untold sums, tens of billions of dollars. They have turned the presidency into a family business so effectively that every one of them is now basically a billionaire in their own right. Melania and her documentary. Barron and his crypto scams and his relationship with the Tate brothers. It goes on and on. These people have made staggering amounts of money while Donald Trump has held the most powerful office in the world.

And I don't give a shit whether somebody had an official title in the administration. That's not the standard.

If you're the president's wife, his son, his daughter, his son-in-law -- if you have extraordinary access to the President of the United States while simultaneously making enormous amounts of money -- I want to know where that money came from. I want to know who paid it and I want to know what they wanted. All of it should be looked at.
Before anyone accuses me of partisanship, let me be clear: I'm being consistent. I never had a problem with people investigating Hunter Biden and Burisma. If Hunter abused his position to profit off his father's office, I want to know, and I want him held accountable. That's how this is supposed to work.
But let's not pretend the scale is remotely the same. Whatever Hunter Biden did is a hot day in Arizona. What the Trump family has done is the surface of the goddamn sun.
What surprised me was the reaction. All weekend, I heard the same thing: "Come on. Barron's just a kid."
No. He is not a kid. He's a grown-ass man, participating in the adult world and making his own decisions. His best friend is a world-famous human trafficker. And he's involved in the his family's cryptocurrency business. World Liberty Financial isn't some lemonade stand his dad helped him set up. Forbes estimated that the Trump family had already pocketed roughly $780 million from World Liberty by September 2026, with Barron's own fortune estimated at $150 million -- much of it tied to crypto. The venture has also attracted major foreign investment.
And apparently crypto wasn't enough. Barron is also a director of SOLLOS, a privately held yerba mate startup that has raised around $1 million -- because nothing screams "perfectly normal presidential-family business venture" like another Trump company where we have very little visibility into who owns what or what Barron's stake actually is.
So yes, put it _all_ under a microscope.
Barron doesn't get a different set of laws because his father happens to be president. Thinking otherwise is exactly the kind of special treatment that got us here.
I'm sick of watching these people hide behind age, gender, or whatever shield is convenient that week. Melania doesn't get extra protection because she's a woman. If she's complicit in the self-dealing inside this administration, she answers for it like anyone else would.
And neither of them gets a pass because they don't have an office in the West Wing. That's the entire point. You don't need an official government title to benefit from proximity to power.

Melania has her documentary. Barron has crypto. If money is flowing to members of the president's immediate family while he controls the United States government, I want to know who's paying it, what access they have, and what they might be getting in return.
And then there are Don Jr. and Eric. Their business interests don't exist in some alternate universe disconnected from their father.

Don Jr.'s venture capital firm took a stake in Vulcan Elements. Roughly three months later, the Pentagon announced a $620 million loan to the company. That doesn't prove a crime. It does mean Congress should be crawling all over it.

Same with Ivanka. Same with Jared Kushner. If Jared is raising billions of dollars from Middle Eastern governments while simultaneously operating in the orbit of American foreign policy, "technically he's a private citizen" doesn't end the conversation.

That's where the conversation starts.
Because this is bigger than one family. We are living through a period of American history where an entire class of people faces essentially zero accountability, and that is not a partisan problem. There are Democrats in the Epstein files who have never been held accountable. There are Republicans in the Epstein files who have never been held accountable. Wall Street was never truly held accountable for 2008, and I'd argue a huge share of the rage tearing this country apart traces straight back to that failure. That isn't left or right. That's American.
And here's what's about to happen.
They're going to scurry away like rats. An unprecedented number of staff are already sprinting for the exits of this administration. They're leaving because they're betting that nobody writes down their names. They're betting nobody will remember how they used their positions to get close to powerful people, to land the next cushy gig, to cash in on the way out the door.
They're betting we forget.
I haven't forgotten. I want to know what the hell happened with Tom Homan and that $50,000 bribe. I want to know about Eric Trump trying to get confidential information to rig UFC matches in front of the White House. Hell, I'm still mad about Brett Kavanaugh's near two hundred thousand dollars of credit card debt. We were told it was for multiple packages of Washington Nationals season tickets and that his 'handful of friends' had paid him back, and then it just vanished. Who paid it off? I still want an answer to that too.
These stories don't get to evaporate because the news cycle moved on.
If there is no gravity in Washington, no accountability for anybody, from the President of the United States, to his wife, to his kids, to members of Congress, to his cabinet, Democrat or Republican, then we don't really have a country anymore. We have a banana republic. And banana-republic corruption doesn't fix itself. It has to be rooted out, root and stem.
I don't care about the pardons. I don't care about the excuses. I don't care how old anyone is or how sympathetic they look on camera. I care about one thing: proving to the American people that a functioning democracy and a functioning justice system still hold powerful people accountable for the damage they've done, the money they've stolen, and the lives they've ruined.
Because the next time a group of people thinks they can loot this country and abuse the power we entrusted to them, they should stop and think twice. They should remember exactly what happened to the last group that tried it.
That only happens if we keep the receipts and act on them.
With urgency,
--Mike

# [Chick-fil-A keeps humans at the drive-thru as rivals go AI](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Chick-fil-A CEO Andrew Cathy said the chain[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/79108bfc-0173-45cf-9f5c-e6b0e5a04326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[will not let AI take drive-thru orders,](https://substack.com/redirect/79108bfc-0173-45cf-9f5c-e6b0e5a04326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/79108bfc-0173-45cf-9f5c-e6b0e5a04326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)even as McDonald's prepares to test voice ordering and Wendy's rolls out Google Cloud's FreshAi.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Human hospitality:** Cathy told CNBC the drive-thru should stay "human to human," adding, "We're not going to substitute that interaction with technology," because that hospitality creates a warm environment.
* **Rivals testing:** McDonald's plans to test Archy voice ordering in English and Spanish. Wendy's is deploying FreshAi, built with Google Cloud, to improve speed, accuracy and consistency.
* **Behind the counter:** Chick-fil-A is still exploring AI away from the speaker. A 2024 Georgia site uses four lanes and a conveyor that can deliver a meal to staff every six seconds.
* **Scale of the call:** The private chain posted about $23.9 billion in U.S. systemwide sales in 2025. Cathy said drive-thru orders stay with employees even as the company tests other ways to serve guests.

# [Spain's left gambles the government on a Nov. 29 vote](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez **[called a Nov. 29 snap election](https://substack.com/redirect/7f37c2a2-3f2c-469e-9dad-d9383b62cb43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Monday after parliament killed his emergency housing package, betting rent anger **[can save a Socialist government that trails in the polls.](https://substack.com/redirect/c21ce92e-0c6b-4e4a-9d9e-27078266e40e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Housing package failed:** Rejected measures would have paused evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, raised taxes on tourist apartments, extended pre-2028 leases by two years, and limited investment-firm home buys.
* **Street and China:** Protests followed September's eviction of an 87-year-old disabled woman from a home of 70 years. Consello said a right government could drop Spain's softer China line and reopen NATO spending.
* **Polls and odds:** A 40dB poll had opponents PP at 31.6%, PSOE at 27.4% and Vox at 18.4%. Eurasia sees a 70% chance of a center-right majority. Sanchez has not passed a budget in more than three years.
* **Bond market shrug:** **[Spain's 10-year was little changed at 4.08%](https://substack.com/redirect/4b3fef48-6713-4e41-bf25-ff726568e61e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, and the spread widened 3 basis points to 65. Goldman said the ECB bar is lower for an "innocent bystander" like Spain than for France.

# [Goldman co-CEO: cut spending or yields keep climbing](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs International co-CEO Anthony Gutman **[said Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/f07ce669-4e34-4fd7-b101-8a9941825d21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that lower deficits and more durable growth are[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/24d01c5d-68a9-4169-b1c5-43e12e83cbb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[the only lasting answer](https://substack.com/redirect/24d01c5d-68a9-4169-b1c5-43e12e83cbb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to a Western bond rout now centered on France.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **London warning:** Gutman told CNBC "we need lower fiscal deficits, and we need more durable economic growth," naming energy costs and the labor market as the drivers markets are watching.
* **Yield tape:** The U.S. 10-year was last at 5.2581%. **[France's](https://substack.com/redirect/70d7102d-a5d5-45ab-b90f-4de2c999b73d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** 10-year stood at 4.8812%, a Friday high since 2002, with debt at 119% of GDP and a 340 billion euro 2027 borrow planned.
* **Not a crisis yet:** TD said "a fiscal apocalypse is not upon us just yet," seeing interest near $1.1 trillion this year. BMO said the rise has "largely been a real rates story."
* **Euro and spread:** The **[Euro touched $1.1160, weakest since May 2025,](https://substack.com/redirect/9886a7ac-b10e-4a69-b21c-f01b9c914113?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** then sat at $1.1176. The OAT-Bund spread ended the week at 140 basis points, a 34 point gain and the largest in 17 years.

| | | **We are less than 29 days from Election Day, and South Central Texas cannot afford to send another Trump-backed yes-man to Congress. ** I was born and raised on the West Side of San Antonio by a hard-working mom who taught me what it means to work hard. And with Washington politicians like Bryan Steil disconnected from reality, folks really appreciate that kind of honesty. Folks, it's easy to be cynical about politics these days. But candidates like Mitchell, who are everyday people ready to take on corporate MAGA yes-men like Bryan Steil, give me hope. If you agree, we need your help. If you have saved your information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process instantly. | | | **** | ** | | ** | ** | | ** | ** With care, Brett Mitchell Berman's Campaign Manager | | | | Mitchell is a devoted husband, father of two girls, and Packers season ticket holder who still believes in the promise of the American Dream—even as that dream becomes harder to reach for so many. With more than 23 years of experience in healthcare, Mitchell is a registered nurse who has spent over a decade serving veterans, active duty servicemembers, and their families at the VA. He never thought he’d run for office, but he’s running for Congress because he’s sick of the corrupt career politicians in Washington who are enriching themselves and their big donors at the expense of regular people, and he believes we deserve a system that puts our health and well-being first, not corporate profits. Mitchell is challenging the Republican incumbent Bryan Steil, a career politician and former corporate lawyer, and he needs you on his team to win. Prefer to donate via mail? Address a check to:** Mitchell Berman for Congress PO Box 44181 Racine, WI 53404 | | Paid for by Mitchell Berman for Congress Mitchell Berman was an RN at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Contribute $15 or more today to help us reach as many voters as possible before November >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/w_ %%%FIRST NAME%% — we just got results from testing we conducted on voter
persuasion and turnout campaigns over the summer, and this could be the key to winning the midterms. In three different House races in Michigan, Virginia, and Arizona, we connected
with voters about how their Republican members of Congress voted to cut clean
energy projects, driving up their utility bills. We ran tests before and after polling, and the results were shocking — the strategy improved polling for pro-environment candidates by four points.

truly impacted these individual races and this change was not because of larger
national trends. A consistent four-point swing is enough to turn a losing race into a winning
one. It’s enough to transform a close election into a landslide. The question now is simple: can we scale up fast enough to make the difference? We need your help.We’re hoping to reach hundreds of thousands of households with best-in-class
canvassing. This means going door to door to turn out voters who will decide who
controls Congress in 2026. Please, rush your urgent contribution of $15 or more today. We need your help to scale up our work in key states and districts ahead of November’s elections >> https://links.messages.lcv. Here’s what our research showed: our messages, which included testimonials from
real voters, were eye-opening. When people hear about how Republicans cut clean
energy — and the impact on their utility bills — it swings their votes in a
major way. By leveraging clean energy affordability, we’re able to reach voters who may not
hear from a Democratic campaign, and these “Energy Bill Voters” will decide the

In 2014, I took a team into Liberia while Ebola was killing thousands, because that was the mission and somebody had to go. **I never served with a single weak person in 40 years.** Not the young soldiers who walked patrols knowing what could be waiting for them. Not the medics, mechanics, and cooks who kept us alive and moving. Not the military families who held everything together at home while we were gone. So who does Pete Hegseth think he is? **Our armed forces have never been weak. Not under any president or any party. Those men and women were strong long before he got a podium, and they'll be strong long after he's gone.** Northwest Georgia is full of veterans and military families who know that truth. They deserve a representative who will stand up and say it proudly. Right now, Clay Fuller holds this seat, and I haven't heard him say a word. On November 3, I'm asking voters to send someone to Congress who knows what our troops are made of, because I served with them. **We have 29 days left. Every dollar helps us get this message on TV screens, in mailboxes, and on veterans' doors across the district before Election Day. So I am asking: Can you chip in $25 right now to send a veteran to Congress who will stand up to Pete Hegseth?**

body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi there,

Our first debate is tomorrow, and we could really use your
help.
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/20149?amount=25&t=1001&akid=1952%2E181023%2EgVftrT ]Will you step up today
and make your first generous contribution before Jocelyn takes the
stage?

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/20149?t=1002&akid=1952%2E181023%2EgVftrT ]Donate →

At the end of the day, this race is about one simple question: what do you
want your governor fighting for?

We know what Jocelyn will fight for...

To drive down costs. From the grocery store to the gas pump, from the
doctor’s office to the mortgage bill, far too many hard-working families
across Michigan are struggling to make ends meet.

To help Michigan families build wealth and get good-paying jobs in the
state. That means a Michigan where teachers can afford to live in the
communities they teach in, and nurses are paid well and taken care of in
the workplace.

To prepare Michigan to defend our rights, our freedoms, and our democracy.
As Secretary of State, Jocelyn has spent years standing up to attacks on
our democracy and defending our elections. As governor, she’ll continue
fighting for Michiganders — regardless of who’s in the White House.

We think the choice is clear. Michiganders need a
governor who cares about making their lives better — and that’s Jocelyn.

But we’ll be honest, running a campaign that works for the people isn’t an
easy feat. It takes everyone doing whatever they can in the moments when
it matters most. And this is one of those moments.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/20149?amount=25&t=1003&akid=1952%2E181023%2EgVftrT ]That’s why we’re asking: will you please chip in your
first donation today to help elect a governor who will
fight tooth and nail to make real change for Michigan families?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

Peter,
_**For 45 days, a 12-year-old girl lived through a nightmare no child should ever experience.** _ She had been trafficked, drugged, abused, and held against her will in a homeless encampment in California. **For 45 days, it seemed as if everyone had forsaken her.** **For 45 days, she suffered a living hell.** **For 45 days, she endured untold horrors.** [ _**Then came Day 46. That was the day our team at Heroes for Humanity went in and brought her out.** _ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=69a7de60fee744aaa42ccb6206206873&_e=QTTEaAPWUXZfkUQYsYb8NI4KG4BANcciuduIqyviizYj4Q1aYU-08H3duIiTKEawBYdEwH82EfdljlnyuTUK4Ac6h02h5GoWlcX8sZFvOOAKO1baIAasaF9LNUbwG7f7Zo1jyXeLR0wHwzQM09wrIDvnoK6zAY-JXPAky8XHjkEwuJziC5dVAkE7ySgD_qHdjQeQEUbKVl_wZ9ZLXYlYq2YJIRF_Gp34hWEERBrPYKo5SyDfnsQrFQ1-4NreASbwSLAbaeE6XqZiQZHXIaWrHztA1_OzZatCtMxlPRIH81ticwqw0Yzu5AppMgmZFJ7DUVlSlxis3JouP2HnkNmabyN2czab7kdSaUI-t5DiTQ2jYjWZvAQbSO4fZz1W5w1NH6_ZZAcsOeDLrSQWdf6GpKF1VkI9AX5K5AYenY8XklnbFZLKlb0TKIT-HXvETbP7qGTKK8PKNf19GMr9Vv55e_qjy03zeE0q9OirLjvQOg2V6xMclt6w_reD9oLd1Gb6kA-aWIqUN5RvBnZKZzyhe0hE_l47H1sZ5_MsdPLLWFIvXOF5BFfaYiBRlk0Z6kvqR-VZuxTkevNITvaS9znKU4osY0GFuSyQRgPJdT0Pa5cQzqlopo5mAj49cA_INJ2Sj_hRi0sVaX09Yl9kay6tuFZo93ELoLUgd6LoaXA9ECd1W0zguPVYSXw-e_gP7G7kR--y-tbPVffX3ZuLdNg_7mrdisCq7py1LoRTtYJCoGI%3D)
My name is Dennis Price, and I want to tell you why I'm sharing her story with you today. I believe God puts people in our path for a reason. Sometimes He calls us to pray. Sometimes He calls us to give. And sometimes He puts someone in front of us who desperately needs help, and then the Lord asks, “Who will go?” I have spent more than 19 years across various special operations units and private military contracting, and now I serve as a humanitarian and evangelist. I've seen suffering most people thankfully never will. I started Heroes for Humanity during the collapse in Afghanistan, watching Americans and vetted Afghan allies get hunted while the systems built to get them out failed completely. A small team and I helped rescue dozens of them. **That crucible proved how powerful it can be when good people refuse to look the other way.** We’ve carried that mission to all corners of the world, including responding to devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and Colombia this summer and the deadly Texas Hill Country floods last year. Our team is made up of veteran special operators, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday heroes who are willing to go into the places others can’t – or won’t – to rescue people in desperate need. [ _**For that little girl, it meant getting her out of an unimaginable situation and bringing her home.** _ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=69a7de60fee744aaa42ccb6206206873&_e=QTTEaAPWUXZfkUQYsYb8NI4KG4BANcciuduIqyviizYj4Q1aYU-08H3duIiTKEawBYdEwH82EfdljlnyuTUK4Ac6h02h5GoWlcX8sZFvOOAKO1baIAasaF9LNUbwG7f7Zo1jyXeLR0wHwzQM09wrIDvnoK6zAY-JXPAky8XHjkEwuJziC5dVAkE7ySgD_qHdjQeQEUbKVl_wZ9ZLXYlYq2YJIRF_Gp34hWEERBrPYKo5SyDfnsQrFQ1-4NreASbwS933r5PozwDags2ladkW1hF7uyGNyTXgoTM6fo7k-P3n6da_hbAWGV6-SNdbbTKm5MqivXePqRzCJ5VT7g8YKMXPyXo-TS--B_lyWCZAF3dJd6i9MtIVnAcrzwfnqLcZs61AlMmV5DnYwcVLrf3HC1ixQIcRkKzQddx1EDlAF0LsatIwF-HSD1KgpXeDzbmXJUB8AUqIEDMfKwsZze4P9AokBk1MF4Dqblmt4KxSCHvAIAxzIhDyZ0plrULVAprFPpUJt6qvwtb_kkhOGkz8fKtPzW-TrYcewvjWciBf2chjHa4Zpnl_mMaSnb7BNtrAxW_JlFS-6ado-Wdz1hr90a8bAMEJQGOLg25vwQB81feSgVXSWNxuRV2gU0w_u6ZGrcO1yk57R5OWq80lvmVfq4tU_igkjguK0672M1ETPgqXDnCCqWF-s-uOf3zNwNP6C8gtjpvn0HEuV0ucRazopJ4twf81jOU94Bl71oMm9ks%3D) In other cases, it could mean delivering lifesaving aid after a natural disaster, pulling families from a warzone, or simply being there on the worst day of someone’s life and reminding them that they have not been forgotten. name: Powered by People
subject: This is different
body:
[1]LeftNet

We know you’re probably getting a fair amount of annoying emails from
political campaigns and organizations.

While we can’t speak for those folks, we can tell you that at Powered by
People, we’re working around the clock to reach as many Texans as possible
before election day.

Here’s how we’re different from others in your inbox:

1. We do the work that works. In 2024, 79% of voters in our network cast
their ballots, compared to the 39% average statewide.
2. We’ve spent more than $500,000 fighting Ken Paxton in court to protect
our right to organize and Texans’ right to vote.
3. Beto doesn’t take a salary from Powered by People. He’s a proud
volunteer like thousands of others.

The steps we take today and over the coming years allow us to build
something much bigger than one candidate or election.

[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/22970?source=em20261005-1718&t=1001&akid=1718%2E2118727%2EFfDsZL ]Whether you can volunteer, help register voters, show up at events, or
simply stay connected and help spread the word, there is a role for you —
and we need you in this fight.

In solidarity,

Team Powered by People

#
| | | | | Hi Peter – Roy Cooper here. My friend Sherrod Brown is running for U.S. Senate over in Ohio, and he needs our support. If you can, [**_I hope you'll split a donation between our grassroots campaigns.**_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19285?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1619&amount=5&t=7&akid=4282%2E124072%2E0Nm892)

---|---
Peter, let me be clear: **There is no second place in this race.**
There’s no silver medal, no participation prize – and no "try again next year." Our race in Ohio will decide Senate control, and I can’t stress enough how high the stakes are.
Second place means rising costs for hardworking families.
Second place means cuts to healthcare coverage so that the wealthiest Americans get more tax breaks.
**Second place means giving Jon Husted two more years of being Trump’s puppet – and it means giving up our best shot at flipping the Senate.**
That’s why I need your help, Peter. Right now, we’re tied in the polls, and Republican megadonors are spending a quarter of a BILLION dollars to help Husted surge ahead.
The only way I can fight back is with your immediate help. I’m relying on grassroots support from folks like you to ensure the values and priorities of Ohio working families come in first place on November 3.
[**_Will you split $5 between my campaign and Roy Cooper right now to win in Ohio and flip the Senate? In a race this close, every dollar could be the difference between winning and losing._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19285?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1619&amount=5&t=9&akid=4282%2E124072%2E0Nm892)

| | | | | | Peter,

New Hampshire voters have an important choice to make on Election Day, and we want to make sure you know exactly who is standing up for the principles we believe in.

**Today, Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire is honored to announce our**[**153 endorsements**](https://us.list-manage.com/iCQcezack9D?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)**for the Tuesday, November 3rd election.**

Every candidate we have endorsed has signed [The Pledge](https://us.list-manage.com/2IJF9ylCKBF?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70) and committed to the people they are running to represent to fight for limited government, constitutional freedoms, parental rights, and the values that have made New Hampshire the Live Free or Die State.
**These are candidates who have put their commitments in writing and are asking voters to hold them accountable.**

Last time, it took 22 days. This time, I want to know sooner. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140743146/651373972/-810700128?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTI3ODk3MDktZjNjMC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FNsi0OQtq64KiGxMmMoOn4QuCIwalVm7_fWSvYy9Uug=)
Friend, Starting today, ballots are on their way to every registered voter in CA-45. Election Day is four weeks from tomorrow, but plenty of voters here will cast their votes this week. **[That's why my team set our biggest goal of the final stretch: $25,000 by Sunday night. Will you chip in $3 to help us get there?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140743147/651373973/439559405?refcode=em-10.5.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTI3ODk3MDktZjNjMC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FNsi0OQtq64KiGxMmMoOn4QuCIwalVm7_fWSvYy9Uug=)** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140743148/651373974/439559405?refcode=em-10.5.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTI3ODk3MDktZjNjMC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FNsi0OQtq64KiGxMmMoOn4QuCIwalVm7_fWSvYy9Uug=) The last time I was on the ballot, it took the Associated Press 22 days after Election Day to call this race. We didn't find out we'd won until the day before Thanksgiving. In the end, it came down to 653 votes. Every one of those votes came in on a ballot just like the ones heading to mailboxes across Cerritos, Westminster, and Fullerton right now. I don't want to relive those 22 days of not knowing. I'd like to know a lot sooner this time. The way we get there is by reaching voters while their ballots are still in their hands, and that has to start this week. Hitting $25,000 by Sunday puts our organizers, mail, digital ads, and in-language outreach in front of voters when ballots are still waiting to be filled out. clean_body: Last time, it took 22 days. This time, I want to know sooner. | = Friend, Starting today, ballots are on their way to every registered voter in CA-45. Election Day is four weeks from tomorrow, but plenty of voters here will cast their votes this week. = = The last time I was on the ballot, it took the Associated Press 22 days after Election Day to call this race. We didn't find out we'd won until the day before Thanksgiving. In the end, it came down to 653 votes. Every one of those votes came in on a ballot just like the ones heading to mailboxes across Cerritos, Westminster, and Fullerton right now. I don't want to relive those 22 days of not knowing. I'd like to know a lot sooner this time. The way we get there is by reaching voters while their ballots are still in their hands, and that has to start this week. Hitting $25,000 by Sunday puts our organizers, mail, digital ads, and in-language outreach in front of voters when ballots are still waiting to be filled out. body:
Most campaigns won’t tell you this part

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140744638/651376107/-240735101?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNTgwZTI0ZS1mM2MwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Dbyk8dnZpQMMsVgesN6NknO50pIyr-sNaB5ppJ8ovUI=) Most campaigns won't tell you where your money actually goes. But I want this campaign to be different — so I’d rather just show you: My team and I sat down this week and mapped out exactly what our October will look like: What we can afford, what we can't, and what it costs to reach one undecided voter here in Kansas' 3rd. | | | Welcome back to the WFP newsletter, Peter! **Primary season is officially in the rearview mirror, and WFP champions are heading into November with serious momentum.** With Election Day just weeks away, there's a lot to catch up on, so let's dive in:
* * *
**_All We Do Is Win Win Win_** First up: a victory lap! Our final primaries brought more wins in **Delaware** , **Rhode Island** , **Massachusetts** , **Wisconsin** , and **Connecticut** , capping a season in which more than **70 new WFP state legislative candidates** and **19 WFP congressional candidates** won their primaries. They ran on affordable housing, health care, stopping data centers, taxing the rich, and fully funding public schools. **And they won, despite being vastly outspent by Big Tech and big business and running without the institutional support their opponents enjoyed.** Here's the roundup:
* **Delaware:** Remember the Billionaire's Bill? Delaware voters sure did. The corporate law firms that helped Elon Musk secure his $56 billion payout funneled millions into a super PAC to protect the legislators who voted for it. It didn't work. **WFP candidates unseated five incumbents.** **Shay Frisby** (SD-5), **Michelle Booker** (HD-2), **Brandon Fletcher Dominguez** (HD-3), **Pamela Salaam** (HD-16), and former WFP staffer **Tyeisha Grier** (HD-28) all beat Democrats who voted for the bill. **Rae Krantz** won an open seat in HD-6, **Rep. Sherae'a "Rae" Moore** was re-elected in HD-8, and **Kira Alejandro** won an open New Castle County Council seat. If they win in November as expected, our State House bloc nearly _doubles_ , putting universal free school meals, earned sick time, and rent stabilization within reach.

* **Rhode Island:** Providence rents now rival New York City's, yet the city has _zero_ rent regulation. That's because the mayor vetoed a 4% cap on annual rent increases. So longtime WFP member and state**Rep. David Morales** took him on, promising rent stabilization within his first 100 days. Despite facing more than $2 million in corporate money, David won. And he won't be governing alone:******_all_****six candidates on our Providence City Council slate won their primaries, and we held David's old House seat, too.** Read that again: **the**** _entire_****slate.** That's a governing majority headed to City Hall with the votes to deliver for working people. Statewide, WFP champions won legislative primaries on affordable housing, universal health care, and making the wealthy pay their fair share. That included **Sens. Meghan Kallman** and **Alana DiMario** , who both beat corporate-backed challengers. The business and charter school lobbies spent hundreds of thousands trying to shrink our bloc. Instead, it grew.

* **Massachusetts:** Our brand-new Massachusetts chapter focused on working-class cities that have long been overlooked politically, and it paid off. We swept all three competitive State House primaries in **Lowell** , electing **John Drinkwater** and **Lorena Betts** and re-electing **Rep. Tara Hong**. In **Lawrence** , city councilor and labor activist **Celina Reyes** defeated an incumbent landlord who'd shaped state housing policy (and was indicted for COVID relief fraud). **Ben Ewen-Campen** and **Lora Wondolowski** won open seats in **Somerville** and the **1st Franklin District**. And first-time candidate **Daniel Lander** came within just 34 votes of unseating the Senate President Pro Tempore.

* **Wisconsin: Ismael Luna** (AD-8) beat an incumbent who refused to work with fellow Democrats. **Rep. Ryan Clancy** (AD-19) fended off a well-funded corporate challenger. **Trevor Jung** won the nomination in SD-21, and **Reps. Angelina Cruz** (AD-62) and **Ben DeSmidt** (AD-65) won their primaries.

* **Connecticut:** Five new champions dealt a direct blow to the legislature's corporate-aligned "Moderate Caucus." That's the group that has spent _years_ watering down housing bills and blocking workers' rights. **Maryam Khan** (SD-2) ousted an Education Committee chair who was on the for-profit school industry's payroll. Youth soccer coach **Moise Carelus** (HD-31) took down a four-term incumbent who sided with Republicans to kill gun safety legislation. And public school staffers **Toni Lombardi** (HD-18) and **Angie Parkinson** (HD-10), along with**Jack Fazzino** (SD-13), won open-seat primaries.

These primaries proved that organized people can beat organized money, but none of these wins are final until November. **The same corporate interests and billionaire-funded super PACs we beat are already regrouping for the General Election, and they'll have even more money to spend.** [**Can you chip in to our General Election Fund today and help turn every one of our 2026 primary victories into a seat at the table for working people?**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bk9CWBL6mNySLZi014lfMGm3o6viWCHwuHoOUk3bCwXg_cDQ8-7DbIXtw-4fvF3OPc4jjaUC9sLE_VG4Mg3HOA6tUCbZXk1foBil0CYCM8OfRWuTCy7U-HpC-2Jngw1Q-qvt9grJQizanloiVOQoSrLDbNZ8yLOvX8x5ABT4bQ4jm9wyO2MiOEZd1kiPh_WHHFfvVUt-br9evo506uNxsMi0cDbEAVpmUGptJpb7RLtWooUvBYRUwHnNgF1lspryyY_ZLXiLbccseRefC8XJ7ZqEOEXDJzeGTnUQuBxwJ5DyIZqg3gABXcE1hQCiv701Rp_fyOJoE6q9iKEFiXZQ4e3PtDiQxkIu6G7K_-VLwhCA/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h0/h001.862PXR-0GPZNBGDgk_h5hABxkIzrivrnaZ0SraFWSlA) **[Chip in to help WFP win in November »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bk9CWBL6mNySLZi014lfMGm3o6viWCHwuHoOUk3bCwXg_cDQ8-7DbIXtw-4fvF3OPnTtSe716ayyYPeV3J7jy4-vcinsXfurOu-yfF7e7uVE9Upxdq6fRhP8qgCrsxGablpEgJGJBbzTDj2PhVgViUJ6FLCMmsgU5_8ncXrG7HzZwr0rPqk04YsB4-eIbpPScX4fA51Yl70SWOtbPlsxk7BuizJn4TeOwpD_7s5Rtf_CU1L7Obh3IeGnQKRyTn9TXp1cer7De2naI2oEczM8NGh2LCamUTZUK08sQ7n9k9KquW2gOfarQV7sapZOJepORZYZKIfAeEAPfCfhBm2dpYxVcAiaqDWYwVGtV_vxPEf4/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h1/h001.tPiGywVVH7sMWxNjZGmGxPha6WRMdpm3boMD9-4pYfE)**

**_Practically Speaking, We Can Win the Working Class_** Winning primaries is one thing. Winning in November means reaching working-class voters who've lost faith in both parties. **So how do we do it?** WFP has spent _years_ researching that question, and we've put the answers into our new[ **Practical Handbook for Winning the Working Class.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYd6eLP33O2GRZpvuK-wGuSICB6LWDM9PpJwnPdrmZwZJHxVD4qxXCmnnT-zDi3clqZmvTvxbjBswaMgfjQVqnZzCvAdGFyOOZYyBmeqiuSkPGPxztkV-JunaDdv7fZog5P_7vxuawz04mLtoqtgQv-bo9cv3ee-SnlxKbsZO9EGzo7L3jX2BeVbRSrbBNXl-lNDVnQTx2QHKfBkMfVOepY8kuSx9MdcOBciWaXgRINKKE3M0DaF0yqb8HTf2p_P4x1-jOOAnns9JEtICtgYIM5Rdt7NZMM2bc7o5zfu10lZkWy5ckrMJOjhHV-vIwh-DaeISwaehG_RR_EXbEyx_NCs114W4EeSSGgGJHKbTSm9/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h2/h001.EHaWSbpq0bE880hNNhaCVmnkr2p3XbOwn7DCUMk1TLA) It's a practical guide to the messages that resonate with working-class voters across the ideological spectrum. It covers what helps us defeat MAGA and elect champions who will build an economy that puts working people first. **Whether you're knocking doors or just trying to discuss politics with your uncle, it's worth a read:** **[Read the handbook »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYd6eLP33O2GRZpvuK-wGuSICB6LWDM9PpJwnPdrmZwZJHxVD4qxXCmnnT-zDi3clqZmvTvxbjBswaMgfjQVqnZzCvAdGFyOOZYyBmeqiuSkPy1MbzzKN7VDSOup6mK35aj4OckGrHRwuCeAEntLMT1yxNVl-V2W0r_Sfem1nuNZFapwv1wk6I5ma_-aBXUv73aFMuYDzxaqqxW7b_y9ryS4ABgfAG14X8N2Qg3VaKqdGWoy1ipvrb3advN8icNfAf00mE9LET2UH6Q4mmVJbs5QEmSm0e0I1Vub_Kbzn0kBqJDS4FaKuapnC1CWpgdikpT0j61vJ_07vKBXBZBfuX9hjAcEa0XfuVkjOWhkv1DX/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h3/h001.eUnehb-lsC1t_aTZ3rV9OxqhMyjnmzf9MFKoDROrSYg)**
* * *
**_WFP Candidates Call for AI Safeguards_** One issue that's firing up working-class voters across the spectrum? **Reining in Big Tech.** Last month, AI researchers sounded the alarm that the technology they're building could spiral out of control. They're not the only ones worried. **WFP candidates for Congress responded by calling for emergency regulations and safeguards on AI.** Here's what they had to say:
* [**Will Lawrence (MI-7)**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.IrwCNRMzSkXvFsTjBP9k2H_ppJrr476zIwPYDoGYBwjKmjX3JJ6WiGnEBdIrIBKCtFvyyqo_SDTwvvNfqHj-uyahsu5UeFma9NS_KRdeUUxcXqM-MaBwNpHFxnCAkphn-3qDBsxYQ7N7J1OnOJd0agDC5RMOrnOlDrQYqqhd4YO4d9CPMYm3aGJw_Zh8fLSJ_uXrrqedUj29dWXMrYfl5rORU5rB5HnllRxtn5TCxTL792odHK_vjmKVvRmCYrguahzKQZfZMpYd7yMLU38ljn5YatgijxO_gy7jNtdRHldCfmqq0O1_GuhVc9_p8Y6y-7b4t9jCXBEjBfG_naMqkQ/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h4/h001.zi04oAmV2U-k_rOFkVa_fEDeVOx9Y0wctJNQ6jHcdsI): "Big Tech doesn't have the right to gamble with our jobs and our lives. We need a pause on the development of advanced AI models and a moratorium on new data center construction."
* [**Justin J. Pearson (TN-9)**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.IrwCNRMzSkXvFsTjBP9k2O6q8ILSh7y1bIQLkwNWWkHAAv57AYe4HXQoPGBJMtMH4Btg2lz_pyah6wbLASKMlk085j76C7VJzdBPtbc06rPQOzwb28IOTbJ6tPzx8CPOWTQdrF32OuiR_3K_pfPbA7hk8hC6-VcUYuE4V4vNTYj6aFVFpON52JbB450NcsJxyP5A1PwPqw_VEcFc5G8lPGSRObaOXsioeHU3fVx4ixBb7GfOagtUapshG22FYtpoF2EjTB6pYQZ2ZVCbmz8TUKdi1Q2mRFba5_Gs5gYomWGgIBOmg8___809ZNoEZsy6hezaK_ziuzDzXf87DUCo9Q/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h5/h001._1NwPsh3MdhAiwVxnMp_M3ZCd2IMA3UkxwFzc2PHiFc): "AI companies will not regulate themselves... the government must act immediately to stop them. That's what I will do in Congress."

* [**Abdul El-Sayed (MI-Sen)**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.IrwCNRMzSkXvFsTjBP9k2KajwbGj9lsPro4wYTrOWTlonbTN60tEZVV6Y7ffABJvHND5GG68nw7G1fCgzRZmUKINa-smkInBkzqBU2dUVFvSxt9FU3QZ5tKSDVi9lsg5zXOIPNFswzZLcplxJx8kUVmSB8rDs_60C2lk9vUrnvQHvKy6vEuicYYf5c3sTmliPobp3QsE87Tkvt5LtACzPTiY4CsbRWHfb7Vlsv1AFe_8nkuirlG7MZ8JbAHJtJcmDIjMmxqLdxJt6DzfWTnZH3XLaMvl_qV1g8roYoWmmGSvhxkjBV4sp9e66UfFdZTfbQAIHlDHRIc974aiej9pnQ/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h7/h001.QaqZOXZkH3iajv8ejWxuVbRcN_kNuOshil5jCyYXZKM): "How we change the incentives leading AI labs down this path and protect against these existential risks are defining political questions of our time."

We need Congress to regulate this technology NOW."

As WFP's National Press Secretary Ravi Mangla put it, AI billionaires are "driving us toward a future that we may not be able to control, all so they can be crowned the next trillionaire." **That's why we're electing leaders who aren't in Big Tech's pocket.** **It's also why WFP has been at the center of the fight against unregulated AI and data centers all year, Peter.** We've recruited local data center fighters to run for office, launched our Working Families Guarantee to take on AI-driven job loss, helped power Will Lawrence's upset primary win in a race where data centers were the top issue, and more. **Now we're taking that fight to Congress. Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar have introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which would pause the most advanced AI development until it can be done safely.** But to pass, it needs as many members of Congress as possible to sign on, and that means they need to hear from you: **Text CLOSE AI to 30403, or call 833-636-3259** , and we'll connect you straight to your representative's office. It takes less than two minutes. [**You can also chip in to our General Election Fund and help elect a slate of new champions who'll stand up to Big Tech, rein in this out-of-control industry, and put working families first.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvlwhslwHzsYo7bshL1ic1bk9CWBL6mNySLZi014lfMGm3o6viWCHwuHoOUk3bCwXg_cDQ8-7DbIXtw-4fvF3OPDzHCup53r9-rfBNYYnYZlNB81W36iUs99DltAbJxPIVgNPD_ZJkFJG8IjMYYd-_g1wUEiPivDkKSeTf-1MAjMevEGqS9myespvC4XCARx1HZ6t9vUy7ckdGLETb4pQV-cQwlife6RnCIi-wHXzk_V5cqs6dGgOozf_MvHlCzOXmJGmejfywXeuQURGQjWasDq2BAtJMUba5ZzQSYjYxI6HKMh7T9jRsV6v-tx0aWARHAlYJts42ZLq50MxV2VskR4yHUS4st1a82fGLbBdxS_Upl9cG_MuRyBz4nj5AdRX4/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h10/h001.SmwUZjx3OzGE-SjuXAh6BIDyD3Sgiz3weIMkAtzqhDo)
* * *
**_Building the Party, State by State_** Taking on Big Tech takes serious people power, and our state parties are building plenty of it. Last weekend, New York WFP brought together members, volunteers, candidates, and champions from across the state for its 2026 convention, joined by Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** , Attorney General **Tish James** , and Public Advocate **Jumaane Williams**. Together, they celebrated this year's primary wins and mapped out the road to November. Voters across the country are looking for a political home that will stand up to corporate power and fight for affordability, and WFP is answering the call. New York joins California, Colorado, Oregon, and other state parties that have held conventions this year to bring members together and build for the fights ahead. **This fall, we're poised to send our largest WFP blocs ever to statehouses across the country and to Washington: legislators who will take on billionaires and corporate power instead of taking their money.** Convention by convention and door by door, we're building the party that can win that fight.
* * *
**_So Many Endorsements, So Little Inbox Space_** All that organizing is paying off on the ballot, too. **We've endorsed**** _tons_****of candidates and ballot measures across the country, so many that if we listed them all, you'd still be scrolling on Election Day.** Here are just a few highlights:
* **Wisconsin:** A Democratic trifecta is within reach, and Wisconsin WFP is going for it. That means backing County Executive **David Crowley** for governor against Trump superfan Rep. Tom Tiffany, plus candidates to flip seats in both chambers. One of them is **Madison Alder** and WFP member **Dina Nina** , who would make history as the first transgender member of the Wisconsin Legislature.
* **Connecticut:** Connecticut WFP endorsed a whopping 82 candidates and is going on offense against Republicans who voted against paid sick leave and affordable housing.
* **Pennsylvania:** Former teacher and volunteer firefighter **Chris Thomas** is running to flip the 24th State Senate District. His plan includes raising the minimum wage, lowering costs, and taking on Big Tech's unregulated data centers.
* **Massachusetts:** Massachusetts WFP is backing **Sen. Ed Markey** and **Rep. Ayanna Pressley** and urging a big **No on Question 3.**
* **Utah:** For the first time ever, WFP is endorsing in Utah! Utah is one of the youngest, fastest-growing states in the country, and voters there are _done_ with MAGA supermajorities that answer to corporate landlords and wealthy special interests instead of working families. So we're backing five champions ready to shake things up: four for the State House, **David Chappell** (HD-62), **Stephen Otterstrom** (HD-21), and Reps. **Rosalba Dominguez**(HD-35) and **Sahara Hayes** (HD-32), plus **Luke Maynes** for Salt Lake County Council.

And again, that's just the tip of the iceberg, Peter. From city councils to Congress, there are WFP champions on your ballot this November. **Meet all of our candidates at**[**wfpus.org/candidates.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.N74h5aIU4LN6X-70141HTf058gpP1gDMAPsZUIAUWwHd4TA0yNgOgf0dsow3FTTOdZNBQ3L23dxjzdVbHJQI9DIsweksO5NSdGiztjm5v-0ylPH6cWgwHFeMXmbO_gxIyQzPCJ8KtCl1g0tvjPe3gz_e1nboJz8f_d_bn25ejs3TYAbl2Tc5ujmlsOC5jJ_4eTg0Mj7ZmkdEGGvadRtpy5TahZ2I_WeOt8z3xJ2DltqrYowQ_ZFkGeQ_gD-29EAk/4um/w95o8dFMQNGBspXpF3TK9w/h11/h001.pAD2RnwvRmNPJjvg7il0tPJgxp8SqbbHEDhRNDnK3X8)
