clean_body: | | | Welcome back to the WFP newsletter, Peter! Primary season is officially in the rearview mirror, and WFP champions are heading into November with serious momentum. With Election Day just weeks away, there's a lot to catch up on, so let's dive in: All We Do Is Win Win Win First up: a victory lap! Our final primaries brought more wins in Delaware , Rhode Island , Massachusetts , Wisconsin , and Connecticut , capping a season in which more than 70 new WFP state legislative candidates and 19 WFP congressional candidates won their primaries. They ran on affordable housing, health care, stopping data centers, taxing the rich, and fully funding public schools. And they won, despite being vastly outspent by Big Tech and big business and running without the institutional support their opponents enjoyed. Here's the roundup: Delaware: Remember the Billionaire's Bill? Delaware voters sure did. The corporate law firms that helped Elon Musk secure his $56 billion payout funneled millions into a super PAC to protect the legislators who voted for it. It didn't work. WFP candidates unseated five incumbents. Shay Frisby (SD-5), Michelle Booker (HD-2), Brandon Fletcher Dominguez (HD-3), Pamela Salaam (HD-16), and former WFP staffer Tyeisha Grier (HD-28) all beat Democrats who voted for the bill. Rae Krantz won an open seat in HD-6, Rep. Sherae'a "Rae" Moore was re-elected in HD-8, and Kira Alejandro won an open New Castle County Council seat. If they win in November as expected, our State House bloc nearly doubles , putting universal free school meals, earned sick time, and rent stabilization within reach. Rhode Island: Providence rents now rival New York City's, yet the city has zero rent regulation. That's because the mayor vetoed a 4% cap on annual rent increases. So longtime WFP member and stateRep. David Morales took him on, promising rent stabilization within his first 100 days. Despite facing more than $2 million in corporate money, David won. And he won't be governing alone:**allsix candidates on our Providence City Council slate won their primaries, and we held David's old House seat, too. Read that again: the entireslate. That's a governing majority headed to City Hall with the votes to deliver for working people. Statewide, WFP champions won legislative primaries on affordable housing, universal health care, and making the wealthy pay their fair share. That included Sens. Meghan Kallman and Alana DiMario , who both beat corporate-backed challengers. The business and charter school lobbies spent hundreds of thousands trying to shrink our bloc. Instead, it grew. Massachusetts: Our brand-new Massachusetts chapter focused on working-class cities that have long been overlooked politically, and it paid off. We swept all three competitive State House primaries in Lowell , electing John Drinkwater and Lorena Betts and re-electing Rep. Tara Hong. In Lawrence , city councilor and labor activist Celina Reyes defeated an incumbent landlord who'd shaped state housing policy (and was indicted for COVID relief fraud). Ben Ewen-Campen and Lora Wondolowski won open seats in Somerville and the 1st Franklin District. And first-time candidate Daniel Lander came within just 34 votes of unseating the Senate President Pro Tempore. Wisconsin: Ismael Luna (AD-8) beat an incumbent who refused to work with fellow Democrats. Rep. Ryan Clancy (AD-19) fended off a well-funded corporate challenger. Trevor Jung won the nomination in SD-21, and Reps. Angelina Cruz (AD-62) and Ben DeSmidt (AD-65) won their primaries. Connecticut: Five new champions dealt a direct blow to the legislature's corporate-aligned "Moderate Caucus." That's the group that has spent years watering down housing bills and blocking workers' rights. Maryam Khan (SD-2) ousted an Education Committee chair who was on the for-profit school industry's payroll. Youth soccer coach Moise Carelus (HD-31) took down a four-term incumbent who sided with Republicans to kill gun safety legislation. And public school staffers Toni Lombardi (HD-18) and Angie Parkinson (HD-10), along withJack Fazzino (SD-13), won open-seat primaries. These primaries proved that organized people can beat organized money, but none of these wins are final until November. The same corporate interests and billionaire-funded super PACs we beat are already regrouping for the General Election, and they'll have even more money to spend. Practically Speaking, We Can Win the Working Class Winning primaries is one thing. Winning in November means reaching working-class voters who've lost faith in both parties. So how do we do it? WFP has spent years researching that question, and we've put the answers into our new It's a practical guide to the messages that resonate with working-class voters across the ideological spectrum. It covers what helps us defeat MAGA and elect champions who will build an economy that puts working people first. Whether you're knocking doors or just trying to discuss politics with your uncle, it's worth a read: WFP Candidates Call for AI Safeguards One issue that's firing up working-class voters across the spectrum? Reining in Big Tech. Last month, AI researchers sounded the alarm that the technology they're building could spiral out of control. They're not the only ones worried. WFP candidates for Congress responded by calling for emergency regulations and safeguards on AI. Here's what they had to say: : "Big Tech doesn't have the right to gamble with our jobs and our lives. We need a pause on the development of advanced AI models and a moratorium on new data center construction." : "AI companies will not regulate themselves... the government must act immediately to stop them. That's what I will do in Congress." : "We need to pause the development of ASI and pass aggressive AI regulations now." : "How we change the incentives leading AI labs down this path and protect against these existential risks are defining political questions of our time." : "The risk of AI is a generational one." : "AI companies cannot be trusted to police themselves. We need Congress to regulate this technology NOW." As WFP's National Press Secretary Ravi Mangla put it, AI billionaires are "driving us toward a future that we may not be able to control, all so they can be crowned the next trillionaire." That's why we're electing leaders who aren't in Big Tech's pocket. It's also why WFP has been at the center of the fight against unregulated AI and data centers all year, Peter. We've recruited local data center fighters to run for office, launched our Working Families Guarantee to take on AI-driven job loss, helped power Will Lawrence's upset primary win in a race where data centers were the top issue, and more. Now we're taking that fight to Congress. Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar have introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which would pause the most advanced AI development until it can be done safely. But to pass, it needs as many members of Congress as possible to sign on, and that means they need to hear from you: Text CLOSE AI to 30403, or call 833-636-3259 , and we'll connect you straight to your representative's office. It takes less than two minutes. Building the Party, State by State Taking on Big Tech takes serious people power, and our state parties are building plenty of it. Last weekend, New York WFP brought together members, volunteers, candidates, and champions from across the state for its 2026 convention, joined by Mayor Zohran Mamdani , Attorney General Tish James , and Public Advocate Jumaane Williams. Together, they celebrated this year's primary wins and mapped out the road to November. Voters across the country are looking for a political home that will stand up to corporate power and fight for affordability, and WFP is answering the call. New York joins California, Colorado, Oregon, and other state parties that have held conventions this year to bring members together and build for the fights ahead. This fall, we're poised to send our largest WFP blocs ever to statehouses across the country and to Washington: legislators who will take on billionaires and corporate power instead of taking their money. Convention by convention and door by door, we're building the party that can win that fight. So Many Endorsements, So Little Inbox Space All that organizing is paying off on the ballot, too. We've endorsed** tonsof candidates and ballot measures across the country, so many that if we listed them all, you'd still be scrolling on Election Day. Here are just a few highlights: Wisconsin: A Democratic trifecta is within reach, and Wisconsin WFP is going for it. That means backing County Executive David Crowley for governor against Trump superfan Rep. Tom Tiffany, plus candidates to flip seats in both chambers. One of them is Madison Alder and WFP member Dina Nina , who would make history as the first transgender member of the Wisconsin Legislature. Connecticut: Connecticut WFP endorsed a whopping 82 candidates and is going on offense against Republicans who voted against paid sick leave and affordable housing. Pennsylvania: Former teacher and volunteer firefighter Chris Thomas is running to flip the 24th State Senate District. His plan includes raising the minimum wage, lowering costs, and taking on Big Tech's unregulated data centers. Massachusetts: Massachusetts WFP is backing Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Ayanna Pressley and urging a big No on Question 3. Utah: For the first time ever, WFP is endorsing in Utah! Utah is one of the youngest, fastest-growing states in the country, and voters there are done with MAGA supermajorities that answer to corporate landlords and wealthy special interests instead of working families. So we're backing five champions ready to shake things up: four for the State House, David Chappell (HD-62), Stephen Otterstrom (HD-21), and Reps. Rosalba Dominguez(HD-35) and Sahara Hayes (HD-32), plus Luke Maynes for Salt Lake County Council. And again, that's just the tip of the iceberg, Peter. From city councils to Congress, there are WFP champions on your ballot this November. Meet all of our candidates at Upcoming Events Of course, endorsements don't win elections. People do. With Election Day just around the corner, here's how to plug in this month: The battleground races we're calling will decide who controls Congress for the next two years. First-timer? No problem. We'll give you training! Remember Justin J. Pearson, who won the Democratic primary for Congress under Tennessee's new Republican map? Now he faces a Trump-endorsed Republican in Novembe.r This month, California WFP and Future is Color are hitting the road with the Big Bad Wolf Tour, three cities, three nights of local artists and DJs, and rooms packed with people who are done being told to be scared. The billionaires have their super PACs, but we have something they can't buy: each other. With Election Day just weeks away, we're turning up the music and building the movement that'll knock on every door between now and November. \- San Diego: Saturday, October 10, at the Soap Factory in Barrio Logan \- San Francisco: Friday, October 23rd at the DNA Lounge \- Los Angeles: Saturday, October 24th, at the Dusty Vinyl Randy Villegas, a teacher and son of farmworkers, is running for Congress to flip California’s 22nd district — one of the must-win seats that will decide control of the House. New to WFP, or been around a while and want to dig in deeper? We'll get concrete about how we're building power in this moment and help you find the best ways to get involved. Photos of the month NYWFP joined the West Indian Day Parade in Brooklyn with drums, flags, dancing, and louding up di vote to gear up for the midterms! That's a wrap for this month, Peter! Election Day is just weeks away, and MAGA Republicans, corporate super PACs, and Big Tech billionaires are spending whatever it takes to keep working people out of power. | | Peter,

The November election is going to be more competitive than people think.

_**Despite the chaos that Donald Trump and the Republican Party have caused in our state, polls show that they're still holding onto some of the political gains they made in 2024.**_

With only weeks left until Election Day, and billionaire-funded outside Republican groups spending millions on races statewide, we need to do what we can to help Democrats up and down the ballot.

**Peter, stopping Republican momentum needs to be our focus.**

Attorneys General count on strong partners at every level of government to pass legislation that supports our efforts to keep our communities safe, stand up for working families, seniors and consumers, and protect our environment from corporate polluters.

The work we do now will set us up for success in the future.

[**Peter, can you chip in $10 or any amount that you can today and join us in supporting Democrats across Oregon in the November election?**](https://us.list-manage.com/16EBodBEpVd?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)

Dan Rayfield
---
| | | | Since taking office as Oregon’s Attorney General in 2025, Dan Rayfield has focused on protecting Oregon’s working families and homegrown small businesses by taking on pharmaceutical companies, polluters, and large corporations driving up costs for groceries and other everyday needs. He’s been fighting hard to block the Trump Administration from taking away the rights of Oregonians, suing Trump–and winning–dozens of times.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/CmQYzR_sNp5?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)

Dan grew up in Oregon and is a product of the Oregon public school system. Following his graduation from Tigard High School, Dan attended Western Oregon University and then earned his law degree from Willamette University College of Law. In 2005, prior to his law school graduation, he clerked for the Benton County District Attorney’s office. During his time at the District Attorney’s office, he gained his first trial experience prosecuting DUIs and other misdemeanor charges. Dan has also served as a coach attorney for the OSU Mock Trial Team, a former Linn County Peer Court Judge, and Past President of the Linn-Benton Bar Association.

Since 2015, Dan served as the State Representative for Oregon House District 16, which encompasses the cities of Corvallis and Philomath, and Oregon State University. In 2022, he was elected by his colleagues to serve as Speaker of the House. Over that time, he helped lead the way on issues including a high quality education for our children, access to affordable and reliable healthcare, making sure families are able to earn a living wage while simultaneously nurturing innovation and supporting Oregon’s small businesses, and making our public safety system more effective and accountable. Dan lives in Corvallis with his wife Amanda and their son Adam.

During his time at the District Attorney’s office, he gained his first trial experience prosecuting DUIs and other misdemeanor charges. Dan has also served as a coach attorney for the OSU Mock Trial Team, a former Linn County Peer Court Judge, and Past President of the Linn-Benton Bar Association. Since 2015, Dan served as the State Representative for Oregon House District 16, which encompasses the cities of Corvallis and Philomath, and Oregon State University. In 2022, he was elected by his colleagues to serve as Speaker of the House. Over that time, he helped lead the way on issues including a high quality education for our children, access to affordable and reliable healthcare, making sure families are able to earn a living wage while simultaneously nurturing innovation and supporting Oregon’s small businesses, and making our public safety system more effective and accountable. Dan lives in Corvallis with his wife Amanda and their son Adam. Prefer to donate via mail? The New York Times last polled our race 3 months ago and found us down 7. This poll has swung 10 points since then.

| | | In June, the _New York Times_ /Siena poll had me trailing Greg Abbott by 7 points, 51% to 44%.

**Today, that same poll has me ahead, 49% to 46%.**
That's a 10-point swing in three months, from one of the most respected pollsters in the country. It's not a fluke, either. This is the third poll showing us ahead of Abbott, and it's the most recent one, taken after weeks of Abbott's attack ads flooding Texas airwaves. [**_Split $25 right now between Linda Sánchez and my campaign to help us turn this polling lead into a win._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140745535/651379503/-1155644748?refcode=BLU_EM_SAN_2026-10-05_01&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85ODI2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTAzZWY1ZS1mN2MwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8bT2Y49wUsOYwTxWwBCHR3Y_OhRo9-h5dHqYaMlSwEA=)

_**Peter**_ , if I say I’m going to do something... I’ll do it. I’ll beg on my knees, go door-to-door hat in hand, tears in my eyes, if necessary. In 2022, the Retail Association of Nevada (RAN) endorsed MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo.

_So, what happened?_

Since Donald Trump retook office, small businesses have been crushed by rising costs and senseless tariffs. Lombardo said Nevadans should brace for "a little pain" and stood by as Trump’s tariffs wrecked working families across the state.
Aaron challenged Trump's illegal tariffs in court, and he won — securing an order to invalidate these tariffs on consumers and business owners.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140747242/651384529/1328794144?refcode=em20261005&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQwN2M5ZGJhLWZhYzAtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=JzirPPDbBl_vmEjDMMQVMOl6ipdwuI_FDaKoxygXjhY=&emci=377c9dba-fac0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=407c9dba-fac0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=4823105)
---
Remember when I paid a visit to Commerce City, Colorado in 2024? [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140747243/651384530/533689903?refcode=em20261005&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQwN2M5ZGJhLWZhYzAtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=JzirPPDbBl_vmEjDMMQVMOl6ipdwuI_FDaKoxygXjhY=) Commerce City is home to one of the most polluted zip codes in the country. And the culprit? **Big Oil.** The Suncor Oil Refinery is one of the top polluters in the state, poisoning the air for the surrounding neighborhoods. **And now, the Supreme Court is hearing a case today that would hold Suncor accountable and liable for the billions of dollars of damage it has caused Coloradans.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140747244/651384531/533689903?refcode=em20261005&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQwN2M5ZGJhLWZhYzAtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=JzirPPDbBl_vmEjDMMQVMOl6ipdwuI_FDaKoxygXjhY=) This is one of the very first cases to reach the Supreme Court that could hold Big Oil and Big Gas legally liable for the climate damage and public health hazards they knowingly unleashed. If successful, it could force ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy to pay billions for climate damages their lies helped fuel in Colorado — including right in Commerce City, just blocks from the refinery. What I saw in Commerce City broke my heart. I heard firsthand accounts of what everyday people are facing due to pollution from Suncor and neighboring industrial sites:
* Daily headaches and chronic nosebleeds
* Spiking rates of asthma and respiratory illness
* Devastating cancer diagnoses

But these stories aren’t isolated to Commerce City. clean_body: Holding Big Oil liable for the damages it has caused: | Remember when I paid a visit to Commerce City, Colorado in 2024? = Commerce City is home to one of the most polluted zip codes in the country. And the culprit? Big Oil. The Suncor Oil Refinery is one of the top polluters in the state, poisoning the air for the surrounding neighborhoods. And now, the Supreme Court is hearing a case today that would hold Suncor accountable and liable for the billions of dollars of damage it has caused Coloradans. = This is one of the very first cases to reach the Supreme Court that could hold Big Oil and Big Gas legally liable for the climate damage and public health hazards they knowingly unleashed. If successful, it could force ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy to pay billions for climate damages their lies helped fuel in Colorado — including right in Commerce City, just blocks from the refinery. What I saw in Commerce City broke my heart. I heard firsthand accounts of what everyday people are facing due to pollution from Suncor and neighboring industrial sites: Daily headaches and chronic nosebleeds Spiking rates of asthma and respiratory illness Devastating cancer diagnoses But these stories aren’t isolated to Commerce City. # MEDIA ADVISORY

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
October 5, 2026

**CONTACT**
Todd Cheewing
Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com

**PRESS ADVISORY: LILY TANG WILLIAMS TO BARNSTORM NEW HAMPSHIRE THIS WEEK WITH STOPS IN JAFFREY, CONCORD, AND TILTON**

WEARE, N.H. — With now less than 30 days until Election Day, Republican congressional candidate Lily Tang Williams will barnstorm the Granite State this week with events in Jaffrey, Concord, and Tilton, including another installment of her _Ask Me Anything _Town Hall series, a candidate policy forum, and a visit with New Hampshire veterans.

TUESDAY, OCTOBER 6 — JAFFREY
“ASK ME ANYTHING” TOWN HALL
Time: 6:30–8:00 PM
Location: American Legion Post 11, 20 Webster St., Jaffrey, NH

Williams will continue her _Ask Me Anything _Town Hall series, taking unscripted questions directly from Granite Staters. The event is free and open to the public.

WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 7 — CONCORD
UNH CARSEY CANDIDATE POLICY FORUM
Time: 6:00 PM
Location: Rudman Center, UNH Franklin Pierce School of Law, Concord, NH

Williams will participate in a one-on-one policy conversation with Pulitzer Prize-winning Washington Post correspondent Kevin Sullivan, followed by questions from the audience.

FRIDAY, OCTOBER 9 — TILTON
COFFEE HOUR AT THE NEW HAMPSHIRE VETERANS HOME
Time: 10:15 AM
Location: New Hampshire Veterans Home, Tilton, NH

Williams will join veterans, their families, and friends for a coffee hour and conversation at the New Hampshire Veterans Home. _**Members of the media are encouraged and welcome to attend all events.**_

**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

body:
A thank-you, a midterm update and some good news.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140747509/651385706/-1038038363?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_NF_Briefing2_261005_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjUyNWU0OTMtZmJjMC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=3ec39RTntouPyr2TP4DJo7fV0fqTLEbYOixZ4RuxB-A=&emci=a695ef57-a8be-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=2525e493-fbc0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=17458827)
Peter,

First, thank you.

Because of you, [_**_Go and Do Likewise_**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140747512/651385711/-1106739200?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_NF_Briefing2_261005_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjUyNWU0OTMtZmJjMC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=3ec39RTntouPyr2TP4DJo7fV0fqTLEbYOixZ4RuxB-A=&emci=a695ef57-a8be-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=2525e493-fbc0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=17458827) is a _New York Times_ , _Southern Independent_ and _USA Today_ bestseller. I wrote this book because I believe deeply that we can heal this country if we remember what the Good Samaritan taught us: everyone is our neighbor. Seeing so many of you embrace that message means more than I can say.

The best part of this tour has been meeting you. I've shaken hands with folks in bookstores and churches and libraries across the country. I've heard stories about your faith, your communities and what keeps you up at night. I’m grateful to everyone who showed up.

Now I'm wrapping up the tour and turning my full attention to the last stretch of the midterms.

In This Together PAC is making a six-figure investment in Kentucky's 6th District to help Zack Dembo. We're also making direct contributions to good candidates in key races across the country.

Let me tell you why I'm optimistic. A year ago, when I was vice-chairing the Democratic Governors Association, plenty of people were worried about Abigail Spanberger and Mikie Sherrill — and they won. We’ve turned a corner. Now we're looking at expanding the map in places like Nebraska and Alaska that weren’t even in play last year.

Why is it happening? Because Democrats are the party fighting to make people's lives better. Folks don't wake up thinking about politics. They wake up thinking about their jobs, their health care and how they’re going to take care of their kids. When we focus on that, we win.

That's exactly what we're doing in Kentucky. Just recently, I announced that [_**we're automatically erasing medical debt**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140747516/651385714/2121166923?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_NF_Briefing2_261005_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjUyNWU0OTMtZmJjMC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=3ec39RTntouPyr2TP4DJo7fV0fqTLEbYOixZ4RuxB-A=&emci=a695ef57-a8be-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=2525e493-fbc0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=17458827) for 130,000 eligible Kentuckians. No family should be crushed by a bill they never saw coming just because someone they love got sick. It’s also going to help improve their credit, so they can get closer to that American Dream of owning a home. And just last week, we announced a historic $10 million investment in maternal healthcare, supporting healthy moms and babies.

That's what electing Democrats this fall can mean for families all over America. So I'd ask you to help spread the word. Talk to your neighbors, your friends, and your family about what's at stake and what we can get done together.

And I'd like to hear from you. Just hit reply and let me know what's on your mind. What are your hopes and predictions for the midterms? How are you helping candidates in 2026? What did you think of _Go and Do Likewise_? All your thoughts and input are welcome.

Thank you for everything you do,

Andy

Trump's unprecedented "midterm convention" wrapped up and it was one of the most sad, pathetic, and dark political events in recent history.
Here are just some of the highlights of the event:

* There were tens of thousands of empty seats in the arena.

* Trump tried to bribe voters by promising $5,000 checks for every American if MAGA wins this November.

* During a speech by Ted Cruz, an audience member shouted "he should be shot" three times at the mention of Zohran Mamdani, James Talarico, and Abdul El-Sayed. Ted Cruz refused to condemn it.

This news changes everything.
**Last week, the Senate Leadership Fund -- a powerful GOP super PAC -- announced they are shifting resources from another state to launch a massive ad campaign here in Kansas in support of my opponent.**
This is a major development. If you still had any doubts that this Senate seat is up for grabs, this news should put those to rest.
What we do now to respond to this news will determine if we win or lose this race. That's why my team and I just set a rapid-response $250,000 goal to make sure we have the resources to fight back. **[Please, can I count on you to chip in at this critical moment?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/049d96f1-030f-43a3-b5f3-851f9accc868?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Why is this happening?_Because Roger Marshall and his allies are terrified of our grassroots momentum._
They've seen the polls tightening.
They've seen the election forecasters upgrading our chance.
They've seen everyone from Nate Silver to Fox News to The New York Times saying what six months ago seemed impossible: We can really flip this Kansas Senate seat.
Now, Marshall's allies are pouring millions into Kansas to stop it from happening. The scary thing is: If we let them outspend us and drown out our message, their plan might work. What breaks my heart is that Kansas families will suffer.
What can we do about it? _We fight back._
We increase our ad buys, up our canvassing and phone banking efforts and make sure Kansans far and wide know that there is a different way forward than the chaos and corruption we're currently seeing from Washington. But all that takes _a lot_ of resources.
We can and must do better for our families, so I am urgently asking: **[Will you please rush anything you can spare to help us fight this latest round of attacks, reach voters across Kansas and WIN?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/049d96f1-030f-43a3-b5f3-851f9accc868?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/049d96f1-030f-43a3-b5f3-851f9accc868?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you SO much for your support -- especially now.
Adam

clean_body: Join a Saturday canvass for Chris Thomas or help us organize to defend the election results. | | Peter, We can help break Republican control of Pennsylvania’s State Senate. But winning will take neighbors showing up, knocking doors, and having the conversations that get people to vote. Our members are organizing for fully funded public schools, homes our families can afford, and wages that cover the bills. In order to get there, we need working-class and Black Pennsylvanians turning out together to elect leaders we can hold accountable to those demands. Chris Thomas is running in the 24th State Senate District to defeat a Republican and help flip the chamber. We’re teaming up with the Working Families Party for upcoming Saturday canvasses to talk with neighbors about this election and why their votes matter. You don’t need door-knocking experience to join us. The training will give you what you need to get started. Bring your commitment to our communities, and we’ll help you put it to work. | | If you can’t make a Saturday canvass, we have another way for you to get involved. Our organizing has to carry through Election Day and the counting of every vote. Working people and Black communities deserve to have our ballots counted and our choices respected. We’re building the collective power to defend both. We’ll identify election protection captains and organize people who are ready to respond if anyone tries to interfere with the results. Preparing together now means we’ll have people ready to lead when our communities need them. Every neighbor we reach and every member who steps into leadership strengthens this movement.Whether you knock doors or join us online, you can help us reach more voters and organize to protect their votes. You have until tomorrow night to submit a comment to protect our national forests. The public comment period on the Roadless Rule closes Tuesday, October 6, at 9:59 p.m. Utah time. After that, the door shuts, and the Trump administration can move ahead with tearing up one of the strongest protections our forests have. It takes two minutes to comment. [Here's a link to a tool I set up](https://substack.com/redirect/090b7d3d-95c7-4ff7-9912-7576f8a25749?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) where you can copy and paste a statement. If you can add a sentence or two about your own connection to these places, that helps a lot.
The attacks on our public lands keep coming. In July, the Trump administration cut Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monuments by about 90 percent. Less than 24 hours later, mining interests started staking claims on land that had just lost its protections. Now the same administration has its sights on our national forests.
Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Z8laIPNp2OhYQJsSNa_NBrFBDSYyYl52tsgH4dQHDc4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=218999482)
The Roadless Rule might be the worst name ever given to a good idea. It sounds like it keeps people out, but it does the opposite. Since 2001, it has kept new roads and commercial logging out of the wildest parts of our national forests, while the trails and roads we already use stay open. It protects about 45 million acres across the country, including nearly 4 million acres here in Utah.
These aren't places on a map to me. They're where I live my life. I ski tour and play in these mountains all the time, from Mineral Fork and Mount Aire to Millcreek, Big Cottonwood, Timpanogos, Mount Nebo, and the Uintas. I've watched the light hit untracked snow in places where the only sound is my skins sliding uphill. The beauty of the Wasatch forest is unparalleled, and many of its wildest corners are protected by this rule alone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f5f44ea3-8055-4f44-bd29-0a7324f7d32b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Caroline Gleich and Rob Lea running on Mt. Nebo. Photo by Louis Arevalo._
A forest isn't something you can patch back together. Once a road cuts through it, the trees come out, the soil washes into the creek, and the quiet is gone for good. Once you amputate part of it, you can never get it back.
The administration says it needs to scrap this rule to fight wildfire. But roads don't stop fires. Roads start them. The Forest Service's own report finds that fires start about four times less often in roadless areas, and it admits any gain in fire prevention would be "modest." The rule already lets crews thin forests and fight fires. Building roads to stop wildfires is like handing out matches to stop wildfires.
And that's not all. The same report lays out the damage:
* These forests feed watersheds that supply drinking water to about 24 million Americans, and repeal would bring more erosion, landslides, and mud into them.
* The plan is "likely to adversely affect" 327 threatened and endangered species.
* Nearby communities could lose up to $9 million a year in visitor spending.
* Tribal nations consulted overwhelmingly oppose repeal, citing threats to sacred sites and treaty-protected hunting and fishing.

Your comment isn't just shouting into the void. It's evidence.
When the government changes a rule like this, everything the public submits goes into an official file called the docket. If the administration scraps the rule and conservation groups sue, that docket becomes the record a judge reviews. Courts don't look at Instagram posts or protest signs. They look at what's in the record.
The law says the agency has to respond to the major concerns the public raises. If we put the facts on the record and the agency ignores them, that becomes the heart of the legal case. They were warned, they had the proof, and they chose not to listen. Judges can throw out a rule for that. Courts also often refuse to consider an argument that nobody raised during the comment period. If it's not in the docket, it may as well not exist.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e37f41b4-f135-4d7a-a4cd-3d6d6def761f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Early morning ski tour in Cardiff, an area protected by the Roadless Rule. Photo by Adam Clark._
Think of it like a home inspection. If the inspector writes down that the roof leaks and the seller ignores it, that report is your proof later. Our comments are the inspection report for our forests.
This has worked before. In 2015, a federal court struck down an earlier attempt to weaken this same rule because the government contradicted its own findings without explaining why.
Comments alone won't win a lawsuit, but without them, there may be no case to make. That's why it matters to name what you care about, whether that's fire, clean water, wildlife, or a trail you love.
Comments close tomorrow, October 6, at 9:59 p.m. Utah time. Please don't wait. Do it now, then forward this to one friend who loves these places as much as you do.
Once we lose these places, we can't get them back. Let's keep them wild. Reach out with any questions or if you'd like more talking points.

# **[Boomers will dump 13.9 million homes and almost none are starters](https://substack.com/redirect/4c2e4ccd-8a36-431e-b8b5-7a0d265dc6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Realtor.com counts 13.9 million boomer and Silent Generation houses likely to hit the tape from 2026 to 2036, up 33.7% on the prior decade. Sounds like a supply miracle. It is not. Only about 380,000 are starter homes with two bedrooms or fewer, 38,000 a year, 3.2% of 2026 starter listings. Retention on starters is 70.7%. They keep the small ones.
* **Winners?** Trade-up buyers. Family homes of three or four bedrooms release about 9.9 million units, near 1 million a year. Large homes release about 360,000 a year. That is real volume.
* **Losers?** First-time buyers still priced out of the only stock they can afford. The silver tsunami skips the starter shelf and leaves the kids the crumbs.
* **Next?** Do not model a starter glut. Model sticky small-home retention and a slow trade-up drip. Home builders who actually pour two-bedroom product still own the scarce seat.

Wall Street loves a demographic fairy tale. This one dies in the bedroom count. 13.9 million doors and 380,000 starters is not a rescue. It is a reminder that boomers die in the house, or sell the big one and keep the condo. Price the scarcity, not the headline.

# **[Japanese capital just called China unwelcome and unsafe](https://substack.com/redirect/4c2e4ccd-8a36-431e-b8b5-7a0d265dc6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Teikoku Databank counts 10,118 Japanese firms still operating in China as of June, a record low since tracking began in 2010, down 22% from June 2024 and about 30% below the 2012 peak. Over two years, 4,137 fully withdrew. Only 1,221 entered, the fewest outside Covid. Topix China profit share is under 15% this year, versus 23% in 2020. The U.S. share rose to 35% from 25%. That is a vote.
* **Winners?** India, ASEAN diversifiers, and Japanese firms that already localized. U.S. re-industrialization just picked up a quiet bid from Tokyo boardrooms.
* **Losers?** China FDI, Japanese China joint-venture earnings, and Beijing's "welcome foreign capital" pitch. Automakers and parts suppliers are first out the door.
* **Next?** The exodus intensifies. Takaichi said in November 2025 Japan could fight over Taiwan. Mineral curbs and August detentions did the rest. Medical and precision stay. The factories do not.

Jeremy Chan at Eurasia Group said Japanese firms and their employees increasingly feel unwelcome and unsafe. He is describing a P&L, not a mood. Tariff risk, cut-throat local competition, and a diplomatic freeze are the same bill. Capital does not wait for a summit to leave. It already left.

# **[Macron and Merz just asked Brussels for a China kill switch](https://substack.com/redirect/4c2e4ccd-8a36-431e-b8b5-7a0d265dc6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
France and Germany want a weapon that does not exist yet. Friedrich Merz and Emmanuel Macron wrote Ursula von der Leyen demanding "powerful measures up to an immediate cut-off from the internal market," activated by reverse qualified majority. The existing toolbox "does not suffice." China is not named. The goods deficit is about €360 billion, near $400 billion. Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič flies to Beijing Thursday. That is the tell.
* **Winners?** EU steel, autos, batteries and machinery if the wall actually goes up. A second-strike tool in days, not the two-year anti-dumping crawl, is a pricing gift.
* **Losers?** Chinese exporters who built a model on the open door. EU consumers who liked the cheap flood. Any German OEM still counting on China volume.
* **Next?** Šefčovič lands in Beijing with a letter in his pocket. Beijing either deals or dares them to build the tool. Reverse qualified majority means the Commission moves unless a weighted bloc stops it.

Europe spent a decade lecturing about open markets while the deficit compounded. Now the two biggest economies want a kill switch with no name. I do not need them to say China. A €360 billion hole says it for them. Own the European names that get a wall. Short the export model that needed the door left open.

# **[Britain just crowned a Temu Range Rover](https://substack.com/redirect/4c2e4ccd-8a36-431e-b8b5-7a0d265dc6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Chery's Jaecoo 7 was the U.K.'s bestselling vehicle in September, 10,813 units, ahead of the Tesla Model 3 at 9,929 and the Ford Puma at 6,958. September moved 350,508 cars, the best September in nearly a decade. The preferred version runs about $50,000, half what it costs for a visually similar Range Rover. It starts near £30,000 and undercuts the Velar by about £26,000. The nickname is the Temu Range Rover. The tape does not care.
* **Winners?** Chery, BYD and the British buyer who wants the look at half price. Jaecoo has sold almost 87,000 U.K. cars. Chery sales more than tripled and passed Ford.
* **Losers?** JLR pricing power, Ford U.K. volume, and every European badge that thought a grille was a moat. Chinese brands took nearly one in six U.K. cars in the first half.
* **Next?** More of this. Almost every sixth British car in the first half was a Chinese brand, higher than any European market except Norway. September Chinese share ran near 23% in one tally. The flood is the product.

Britain did not fall in love with China. It fell in love with a Range Rover shape at half the invoice. JLR can sue the silhouette. It cannot sue the price. The volume already moved.

# **[The SEC just handed retail traders a 3x Bitcoin flamethrower](https://substack.com/redirect/4c2e4ccd-8a36-431e-b8b5-7a0d265dc6c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
On Oct 2 the SEC cleared Cboe BZX to list six Volatility Shares funds built for three times the daily move in Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold, silver, crude and natural gas. Futures, daily reset, no launch date until registration goes effective. Eric Balchunas called it a win. I call it a product the house already knows how to sell.
* **Winners?** Volatility Shares, Cboe, and anyone who understands a one-day instrument. The onshore crypto shelf just got another rung without Congress. BITX and ETHU already proved the 2x shelf sells.
* **Losers?** Anyone who holds a 3x daily reset like a stock. A 10% down day and a 10% up day leaves the coin down 1% and the fund down about 9%. Decay is the business model.
* **Next?** Effective registration, then a launch. Expect the same SEC and FINRA decay warnings, then volume anyway. The 5x filings are already in the pipe.

I said that Trump's crypto team **[would write the rules](https://substack.com/redirect/501c9499-ee93-4c50-8f0b-238956c90717?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while Congress stalls, and Atkins **[paved the onshore path.](https://substack.com/redirect/bf73910b-f673-4f09-a2ab-d708d6e9e06f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** This is that tape. So if your business is generating $25,000 or more a month, Realtor.com counts 13.9 million boomer and Silent Generation houses likely to hit the tape from 2026 to 2036, up 33.7% on the prior decade. Sounds like a supply miracle. It is not. Only about 380,000 are starter homes with two bedrooms or fewer, 38,000 a year, 3.2% of 2026 starter listings. Retention on starters is 70.7%. They keep the small ones. Winners? Trade-up buyers. Family homes of three or four bedrooms release about 9.9 million units, near 1 million a year. Large homes release about 360,000 a year. That is real volume. Losers? First-time buyers still priced out of the only stock they can afford. The silver tsunami skips the starter shelf and leaves the kids the crumbs. Next? Do not model a starter glut. Model sticky small-home retention and a slow trade-up drip. Home builders who actually pour two-bedroom product still own the scarce seat. Wall Street loves a demographic fairy tale. This one dies in the bedroom count. 13.9 million doors and 380,000 starters is not a rescue. It is a reminder that boomers die in the house, or sell the big one and keep the condo. Price the scarcity, not the headline. The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! Musk said "just discussions, but something may come of it." The tape heard the foundry king is in the room. TSM ripped to an intraday all-time high near $486, up about 2.7%, while Intel, the first name on the Terafab dance card in April, got marked down. Terafab is a $16.8 billion Grimes County start that can run toward $119 billion for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. Discussions move stocks. Contracts print cash. Winners? TSMC and anyone long the Musk stack. A role running Texas fabs puts the world's best process next to guaranteed Tesla, SpaceX and xAI demand, off the Taiwan strait. Losers? Intel. April's 14A seat is no longer exclusive. A 2% to 4% hit is the market pricing a two-horse foundry race Elon just opened. Next? No term sheet yet. Watch a supplement-not-replace structure, a Texas campus beside the Arizona build, and Intel forced to prove 14A or lose the volume. I called the Musk industrial complex the bid in again when Westly said a merger was "absolutely likely" in and last week in Terafab is the same trade with a cleanroom. Own the tollbooth. Micron is soft because the crowd wants a memory-price peak. Barron's says the data says the cycle still has room. This is the name that just printed fiscal Q4 sales of $54.23 billion, up 379%, and an 87% gross margin, with Sanjay Mehrotra telling you he has no line of sight to balance. The stock is hovering near $1,070 after a 500% year. Morgan Stanley is still at $1,200, fiscal 2027 EPS lifted to $182.52. That is not a peak. It is a dare. Winners? Holders who fade the peak narrative, HBM customers already locked, and anyone who bought the Jul 1 crown. Single-digit forward earnings on a shortage is the gift. Losers? Shorts betting the 87% margin is the ceiling this quarter. The crowd that sells a shortage because a headline guessed the top. Next? The cycle runs until supply actually shows up. A real peak looks like inventory and a guide cut. Mehrotra says he cannot see either. I in "Wall Street crowns Micron the next Nvidia", "$2 Trillion chip carnage slams into Make-or-Break support", and in "Micron prints 87% gross margins and the crowd still wants a peak." Stay long the memory tollbooth. Sell it when they find the line of sight. Teikoku Databank counts 10,118 Japanese firms still operating in China as of June, a record low since tracking began in 2010, down 22% from June 2024 and about 30% below the 2012 peak. Over two years, 4,137 fully withdrew. Only 1,221 entered, the fewest outside Covid. Topix China profit share is under 15% this year, versus 23% in 2020. The U.S. share rose to 35% from 25%. That is a vote. Winners? India, ASEAN diversifiers, and Japanese firms that already localized. U.S. re-industrialization just picked up a quiet bid from Tokyo boardrooms. Losers? China FDI, Japanese China joint-venture earnings, and Beijing's "welcome foreign capital" pitch. Automakers and parts suppliers are first out the door. Next? The exodus intensifies. Takaichi said in November 2025 Japan could fight over Taiwan. Mineral curbs and August detentions did the rest. Medical and precision stay. The factories do not. Jeremy Chan at Eurasia Group said Japanese firms and their employees increasingly feel unwelcome and unsafe. He is describing a P&L, not a mood. Tariff risk, cut-throat local competition, and a diplomatic freeze are the same bill. Capital does not wait for a summit to leave. It already left. France and Germany want a weapon that does not exist yet. Friedrich Merz and Emmanuel Macron wrote Ursula von der Leyen demanding "powerful measures up to an immediate cut-off from the internal market," activated by reverse qualified majority. The existing toolbox "does not suffice." China is not named. The goods deficit is about €360 billion, near $400 billion. Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič flies to Beijing Thursday. That is the tell. Winners? EU steel, autos, batteries and machinery if the wall actually goes up. A second-strike tool in days, not the two-year anti-dumping crawl, is a pricing gift. Losers? Chinese exporters who built a model on the open door. EU consumers who liked the cheap flood. Any German OEM still counting on China volume. Next? Šefčovič lands in Beijing with a letter in his pocket. Beijing either deals or dares them to build the tool. Reverse qualified majority means the Commission moves unless a weighted bloc stops it. Europe spent a decade lecturing about open markets while the deficit compounded. Now the two biggest economies want a kill switch with no name. I do not need them to say China. A €360 billion hole says it for them. Own the European names that get a wall. Short the export model that needed the door left open. Chery's Jaecoo 7 was the U.K.'s bestselling vehicle in September, 10,813 units, ahead of the Tesla Model 3 at 9,929 and the Ford Puma at 6,958. September moved 350,508 cars, the best September in nearly a decade. The preferred version runs about $50,000, half what it costs for a visually similar Range Rover. It starts near £30,000 and undercuts the Velar by about £26,000. The nickname is the Temu Range Rover. The tape does not care. Winners? Chery, BYD and the British buyer who wants the look at half price. Jaecoo has sold almost 87,000 U.K. cars. Chery sales more than tripled and passed Ford. Losers? JLR pricing power, Ford U.K. volume, and every European badge that thought a grille was a moat. Chinese brands took nearly one in six U.K. cars in the first half. Next? More of this. Almost every sixth British car in the first half was a Chinese brand, higher than any European market except Norway. September Chinese share ran near 23% in one tally. The flood is the product. Britain did not fall in love with China. It fell in love with a Range Rover shape at half the invoice. JLR can sue the silhouette. It cannot sue the price. The volume already moved. On Oct 2 the SEC cleared Cboe BZX to list six Volatility Shares funds built for three times the daily move in Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold, silver, crude and natural gas. Futures, daily reset, no launch date until registration goes effective. Eric Balchunas called it a win. I call it a product the house already knows how to sell. Winners? Volatility Shares, Cboe, and anyone who understands a one-day instrument. The onshore crypto shelf just got another rung without Congress. BITX and ETHU already proved the 2x shelf sells. Losers? Anyone who holds a 3x daily reset like a stock. A 10% down day and a 10% up day leaves the coin down 1% and the fund down about 9%. Decay is the business model. Next? Effective registration, then a launch. Expect the same SEC and FINRA decay warnings, then volume anyway. The 5x filings are already in the pipe. I said that Trump's crypto team while Congress stalls, and Atkins This is that tape. They did not legalize magic. They legalized a daily grenade with a prospectus. Trade the day. Do not marry the product. AI carried the record and the Buy stamp hit 60%. Memory has not peaked. Boomers will not save the starter buyer. TSMC just walked into Elon's Texas fab. Japan is leaving China, Europe wants a kill switch, and Britain bought the Temu Range Rover. The SEC handed retail a 3x chainsaw. | | I'm Dave McCormick. I'm a West Point grad, combat veteran who served in the 82nd Airborne, a 7th-generation Pennsylvanian, **and I defeated an entrenched career politician in the #1 swing state of the 2024 election.**
I’ve seen firsthand what great leadership looks like. I’ve seen that even on our worst days, you have to put the needs of others first.
That’s why I made a promise to come to the Senate and work with fellow political outsiders like President Trump to shake up Washington, and I’m working to do that every single day.
Whether it’s securing the border, reducing crime in our cities, ending the fentanyl epidemic, or bringing down the cost of living–**I’m committed to delivering concrete solutions to the biggest issues we face.**
But in order to get the job done, it’s going to take all hands on deck. I need every freedom-loving American to help me shake up Washington. I promise I won't let you down.
_Senator Dave McCormick_

Friends, things are moving fast on AI and _Congress needs to act._ OpenAI recently disclosed that rogue agents searched federal government websites in ways beyond what they were asked to do. The company also notified foreign governments, universities, and public agencies that may have been impacted. The Australian government confirmed that the OpenAI agents hacked a health service website in June in an attempt to access private data. **This is exactly what happens when powerful technology outpaces the government’s response.** You may be wondering what Trump’s response is to all this... Well, he’s urging Americans to blindly trust that these companies whose rogue agents hacked government websites will “self-police” — that they’ll do the moral and ethical thing, when push comes to shove. That it’s more important that we beat China in this new AI tech race than establish any real rules or guardrails. _But we can’t “win” the AI race if no one trusts these AI systems enough to adopt them — or if they’re actively causing harm to the people who use them._ We need enforceable rules that make AI systems transparent and safe, and hold these companies accountable. “Self-policing” won’t get us there — it’s a recipe for disaster. **I’ve spent years working on AI legislation because I knew moments like this one were coming. clean_body: | | | | = Friends, things are moving fast on AI and Congress needs to act. OpenAI recently disclosed that rogue agents searched federal government websites in ways beyond what they were asked to do. The company also notified foreign governments, universities, and public agencies that may have been impacted. The Australian government confirmed that the OpenAI agents hacked a health service website in June in an attempt to access private data. This is exactly what happens when powerful technology outpaces the government’s response. You may be wondering what Trump’s response is to all this... Well, he’s urging Americans to blindly trust that these companies whose rogue agents hacked government websites will “self-police” — that they’ll do the moral and ethical thing, when push comes to shove. That it’s more important that we beat China in this new AI tech race than establish any real rules or guardrails. But we can’t “win” the AI race if no one trusts these AI systems enough to adopt them — or if they’re actively causing harm to the people who use them. We need enforceable rules that make AI systems transparent and safe, and hold these companies accountable. “Self-policing” won’t get us there — it’s a recipe for disaster. I’ve spent years working on AI legislation because I knew moments like this one were coming. And now, we need urgent action from Congress to put real safeguards on AI before we lose control of this technology — and we need the public to speak up and make their voices heard. The window to get this right is open. Let’s make sure Congress acts. More soon. -Sara = | | | Congresswoman Sara Jacobs California’s 51st District = | = Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress Sara Jacobs for Congress PO Box 120085 San Diego, CA 92112 United States | | | | | | ---|---|--- We believe these emails are a critical way for Sara to stay in touch with supporters and constituents. clean_body: $9 billion in fraud and stolen taxpayer money, rising crime, failing schools.... | | | | | Minnesota has tried one-party control for 20 years, and here’s where that got us: At least $9 billion in fraud and stolen taxpayer money, rising crime, and failing schools. Peggy Flanagan, a failed career politician who enabled the policies that got us here. Her way doesn’t work. And yet we’ve been paying Peggy Flanagan with our hard-earned money for 20 years. It’s not the time to give her a promotion. It’s time to fire her for good. Right now, the “expert” pollsters say she has the edge in this race, but it’s a toss-up that could come down to a few hundred votes on election night. Not only is Peggy as extreme as they come, but she was also Tim Walz’s running mate. She was the sitting Lieutenant Governor during the largest COVID-19 scam in the country – the Feeding Our Future scandal. She’s done everything possible to distance herself from this debacle, and so far it’s worked! We can’t let all the rampant, unprecedented fraud that took place under her watch go unnoticed. It’s a national disgrace. That’s why Tim Walz was forced to end his re-election campaign... Meanwhile, his right hand wants to be our next U.S. Senator. She’s cut from the same cloth as every other Socialist pretending to be moderate today. Peggy Flanagan is a far-Left, extremist politician who will vote to allow girls competing against boys in sports, block voter ID requirements, open up our borders, raise your taxes, and sabotage anything the President wants to do. I’m not a career politician; I cut my teeth at the highest levels of media and sports broadcasting, and my campaign is focused on honesty, common sense, stopping fraud, and doing the small things right. That’s why we are going to win. We have to. Be brave. Do good. – Michele Republican Nominee for Senate, Minnesota | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee.

Hi team,
For the last year I have had the chance to sit down with people from across our part of PA and hear their concerns.
People in **Gordon** , who are concerned about an AI data center being built up on the mountain.
People in **Tremont** , who don't want biosolids stinking up the west end of the county.
People in **St. Clair** , who don't want any more toxic construction material being trucked in on the Burma.
People in **Shenandoah** , who want their costs to go down.
People in **Pottsville** , my hometown, who want to feel proud that we live here.
And it's not just Schuylkill County. Our part of PA has serious issues, and it's time we have someone on the federal level who cares.
**We don 't want our district to be a dumping ground. But that's how Dan Meuser treats it.**
He doesn't live here. He doesn't listen to us. He doesn't represent us.
**[In 29 days, we can give our communities the leadership we deserve. Chip in now to help us get it done.](https://substack.com/redirect/0e7a0f44-b6d8-4e4b-b8b3-14eeec985450?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Rachel Wallace

name: Congressman Vince Fong
subject: With your support, we are delivering results.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vince Fong for Congress
body:
When I ran for Congress, I promised results, not more empty talk from Washington. I want to show you exactly what that's looked like so far. | | |
---
| |
# With your support, we are delivering results.
---
| Friend,

When I ran for Congress, I promised results, not more empty talk from Washington. I want to show you exactly what that's looked like so far. Fighting for our water. I secured $1 billion in western water infrastructure funding, including $540 million going directly to California dams, canals, and water projects. I got $5 million to combat invasive golden mussels threatening our water systems, and delivered local wins for the Pine Flat Dam Raise, Eastman Lake Enlargement, and groundwater recharge projects across Fresno, Tulare, and Kaweah. I introduced the Water Infrastructure Resiliency Act to protect our water systems for the long haul, and I'm still fighting Sacramento's bureaucrats every time they try to take our water away. Standing up for our military and national security. I delivered nearly $98 million for NAS Lemoore's Strike Fighter Center of Excellence and F-35 hangar, and for a new Child Development Center at NAWS China Lake. I secured $39.5 million more for hypersonic testing, rocket lab infrastructure, and readiness programs at Edwards Air Force Base and China Lake, protecting the installations that anchor our local economy and our national defense. Bringing NASA innovation home. My ANCHOR Act, which protects cybersecurity on America's academic research fleet, passed the House 412-11. My ACERO Act, using NASA drone technology to help fight wildfires, advanced out of committee unanimously, 34-0. Cutting the red tape that's driving up your costs. I took on Gavin Newsom's "hidden climate tax" on cargo ships, forced accountability that led the Trump administration to finally pull the plug on California's high-speed rail boondoggle, and I'm pushing back on the State Water Board every time it tries to move the goalposts on Central Valley families. This is what showing up and doing the work looks like. I'm not finished. Not by a long shot. Thank you for standing with me, Sincerely

Congressman Vince Fong

| | Friend, Gas, groceries, and healthcare keep getting more expensive. In northern and central Minnesota, that adds up fast: long drives to work, school, and the doctor with winter heating bills right around the corner.

Choices made in Washington are part of why and **when Rep. Pete Stauber had the chance to lower costs for Minnesota families he voted no.**
* He voted against capping insulin costs at $35 a month for people with private health insurance, including employer plans.
* He voted against the bipartisan infrastructure law, which funded high-speed internet for rural communities.
* He voted against cracking down on price gouging at the gas pump.
* He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut food assistance and shifted millions in costs onto Minnesota counties.

After nearly eight years, too much is still broken. Our representative should be fighting to lower costs for Minnesota families.**Minnesota families are working harder and still falling behind.** Lower prices are only half the answer. The other half is a paycheck that keeps up. Minnesotans deserve fair wages, good benefits, and the security to raise a family. From the mines on the Iron Range to the hospitals in Duluth, Minnesotans should be able to count on dependable work that stays within Minnesota. As your Congresswoman, Trina will fight to bring down the cost of everyday life: working to lower energy costs, pushing back on regulations that raise what families pay for groceries and goods, and standing up for union jobs with wages that keep pace with what life costs. That is what opportunity at home means.

**If you believe Minnesota families deserve lower costs and dependable jobs, join and support Trina’s campaign today.**

---
| | Friend, Gas, groceries, and healthcare keep getting more expensive. In northern and central Minnesota, that adds up fast: long drives to work, school, and the doctor with winter heating bills right around the corner.

Choices made in Washington are part of why and **when Rep. Pete Stauber had the chance to lower costs for Minnesota families he voted no.**
* He voted against capping insulin costs at $35 a month for people with private health insurance, including employer plans.
* He voted against the bipartisan infrastructure law, which funded high-speed internet for rural communities.
* He voted against cracking down on price gouging at the gas pump.
* He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut food assistance and shifted millions in costs onto Minnesota counties.

After nearly eight years, too much is still broken. Our representative should be fighting to lower costs for Minnesota families.**Minnesota families are working harder and still falling behind.** Lower prices are only half the answer. The other half is a paycheck that keeps up. Minnesotans deserve fair wages, good benefits, and the security to raise a family. From the mines on the Iron Range to the hospitals in Duluth, Minnesotans should be able to count on dependable work that stays within Minnesota. As your Congresswoman, Trina will fight to bring down the cost of everyday life: working to lower energy costs, pushing back on regulations that raise what families pay for groceries and goods, and standing up for union jobs with wages that keep pace with what life costs. That is what opportunity at home means.

**If you believe Minnesota families deserve lower costs and dependable jobs, join and support Trina’s campaign today.**

clean_body: Just getting by isn’t a “way of life.”| | | | | Friend, Gas, groceries, and healthcare keep getting more expensive. In northern and central Minnesota, that adds up fast: long drives to work, school, and the doctor with winter heating bills right around the corner. Choices made in Washington are part of why and when Rep. Pete Stauber had the chance to lower costs for Minnesota families he voted no. He voted against capping insulin costs at $35 a month for people with private health insurance, including employer plans. He voted against the bipartisan infrastructure law, which funded high-speed internet for rural communities. He voted against cracking down on price gouging at the gas pump. He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut food assistance and shifted millions in costs onto Minnesota counties. After nearly eight years, too much is still broken. Our representative should be fighting to lower costs for Minnesota families.Minnesota families are working harder and still falling behind. Lower prices are only half the answer. The other half is a paycheck that keeps up. Minnesotans deserve fair wages, good benefits, and the security to raise a family. From the mines on the Iron Range to the hospitals in Duluth, Minnesotans should be able to count on dependable work that stays within Minnesota. As your Congresswoman, Trina will fight to bring down the cost of everyday life: working to lower energy costs, pushing back on regulations that raise what families pay for groceries and goods, and standing up for union jobs with wages that keep pace with what life costs. That is what opportunity at home means. My campaign for governor isn’t just about what happens in 2026 — it’s
about 2028.

If past elections have taught us anything, it's that the path to the
Presidency runs straight through Michigan.

We know this presidential administration will use every lever, as it’s
done before, to try to undermine our elections. We can expect the tired
conspiracy theories they touted in 2020, the same lies my opponent has

stands.

pressure me to turn over the private voting information of voters in
Michigan, I told him: No. I’ll see you in court.

| | Good Afternoon Team Demuth!
**Zoom Meeting**
I want to remind everyone that we will have our regularly scheduled grassroots volunteer meeting tonight at 8:30 PM. We will talk about yard signs, volunteer efforts, some events coming up, and much much more!
I have placed the link below. Once you click the link, you will be taken into a waiting room. I will let you into the meeting from there.
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87316568944
**Update on Right Insight**
Caleb Jungling will be giving a short update on Right Insight and our efforts in knocking on doors and calling phones. This is a fantastic way to help out our campaign. **Even five minutes of phone calling, or door knocking just your neighbors goes an incredibly long way!**
All of you that have previously been volunteers already have accounts. Simply download the app and sign in using the email address you received this message at. You will be sent a six-digit code to verify your identity, then you’re all logged in and ready to roll!For door knocking, we are utilizing a feature called Near Me. This will allow volunteers to go out and door knock houses that are nearby them. That list will change as you move around, so you can use it anywhere.Calls will be broken down by Congressional District. When we add you to Right Insight, we will assign you to calls specific for your area so you are talking to people who you may know, or share more common issues. Most of you will likely see all of them until we are able to organize you into Congressional district teams, so please just call into the CD you are from. For example, if you are from CD 1, call CD1.**If you do login and are told you do not have an account, please fill out the form below and we will get you added!**[ Sign up for a Right Insight Account.](https://us.list-manage.com/EeFBPpKUMj3?e=422536b04e&c2id=3f96188058f7a1407b5cde0c924e7fd7)Both calls and door knocking projects are live and ready for volunteers. We are very excited to get everyone started! If you have technical questions or are unsure of how to get started, please call Caleb at 612-300-4202 or email him at Caleb@mngop.com**Signs** This meeting we will discuss our strategy for the final sign requests statewide and what we are doing to fill them. I will also update everyone on the call to our strategy regarding large signs.We look forward to seeing everyone on the call tonight! Thank you for joining us. With your help, we will elect Lisa Demuth as our next Governor and restore common sense to Minnesota.**Events** We will be updating our volunteers on upcoming events. For example, we have an upcoming Phone Bank Potluck at our Burnsville office this Saturday. From 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM this Saturday, volunteers will bring a dish to share and call for Team Demuth and other Republican candidates! For more information on this event, please call Mary Ander (612) 599-0240 or email at andermary96@gmail.com

Hi there,
I have great news from our latest Ground Truth Weekend of Action: this was our biggest weekend yet—and it was a BLAST.
Together, Swing Left volunteers knocked on **11,096 doors** in **34 swing districts** across **17 states** , from Pennsylvania and Michigan to Georgia, Texas, Washington, and more. _That’s more than double what we did at our last Weekend of Action in September!_
**Among the volunteers who made this weekend such a success were college students from Brown, Yale, Columbia, Harvard, and more who came out to knock on doors:**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/1218?utm_source=em20261005-3039&t=1&akid=3039%2E1562180%2EZ1pUoS)
Between midterm exams, part-time jobs, and everything else that comes with being a college student, these folks chose to spend their Saturday and Sunday deep canvassing.
Alongside them were volunteers of all ages and backgrounds who came together to knock on doors, have deep conversations with persuadable voters, and make the case for Democrats in competitive swing races across the country.
**Here’s just one example of the difference we’re making, from a conversation my teammate Matt had while canvassing in Ohio:**
_“I went to a door with my two kids and talked to a dad. He shared that his son is on the autism spectrum and that it's a struggle to get him the services he needs. He works 12-hour days and is still struggling to get by. He always votes (he feels it's his duty to his kids) but doesn't pay attention to politics and was undecided on the Senate race._
_We connected on concerns about recent Republican education cuts, and I shared Sherrod Brown's long-standing advocacy for working people and families. By the end of the conversation, he said Sherrod Brown was the kind of person we wanted in the Senate.”_
Ohio is a must-win for Democrats’ path to a Senate majority, so conversations like this one, at scale, will make the difference in these close races. That’s one undecided voter moving toward a Democratic candidate, all because someone showed up, knocked on his door, and took the time to listen and talk. And that’s just one example from thousands of conversations we had this weekend!
With less than a month to go until Election Day, we’re working to have _hundreds of thousands_ of conversations with voters before polls close, and there are opportunities to get involved every day between now and then!
**Our next Weekend of Action is coming up on October 17th and 18th, when volunteers across the country will come together for another major push to talk with voters in swing districts and states. But you don’t have to wait until then to get involved. Whether you’re a first-time volunteer or have been volunteering for years, there’s an action for you every single day until Election Day.[Click here to learn how you can take action today.](https://act.swingleft.org/go/1218?utm_source=em20261005-3039&t=2&akid=3039%2E1562180%2EZ1pUoS)**
**[Take Action Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/1218?utm_source=em20261005-3039&t=3&akid=3039%2E1562180%2EZ1pUoS)**
**Can’t join a canvass, but still want to help?[Click here to make a donation to support Ground Truth today.](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl.QSDeHu&refcode=em20261005-3039&t=4&akid=3039%2E1562180%2EZ1pUoS)**
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl.QSDeHu&refcode=em20261005-3039&t=5&akid=3039%2E1562180%2EZ1pUoS)**
Thank you for all the hard work you’re putting into helping Democrats build long-term power this year and beyond. I have been amazed by this community's tenacity and commitment, and I can’t wait to see our work pay off in just 4 short weeks!
Z Mooney
Voter Contact Director, Swing Left

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. They wanted to talk about hospitals cutting services, mothers driving an hour or more to deliver a baby, and clinics that can't recruit enough doctors to keep their doors open.I showed up. Michael Alfonso didn't. = That's the job. You show up, especially when the people asking are the ones holding rural healthcare together. Michael Alfonso had the chance to answer their questions, and he chose not to come. Voters in the 7th District deserve to know where their next representative stands on keeping their local hospital open. And they deserve someone who will be in the room. We have less than a month until Election Day. I'm going to keep showing up in every county, at every forum, and at every town hall. But I need your help to make sure voters know which candidate does. = Thank you for standing with me, Fred P.S. Northern Wisconsin's doctors asked both candidates to show up and talk about rural healthcare. Only one of us did. = | | | Paid for by Clark for Wisconsin Clark for Wisconsin PO Box 385 Washburn, WI 54891 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

### A Biological Chernobyl? It Wasn't Just Predictable. It Was Predicted.
A lab worker has died in Siberia. Nearly 200 potential contacts are under "observation." This, my friends, is sadly the real deal (as if we needed more crap right now).
Reports emerged of a broken test tube containing plague bacteria. That is enough to scramble the jets, so to speak--and demand answers. Darya Shipilova worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute; Russian authorities claim she died from pneumonia of unknown origin and deny finding evidence of a lab accident (uh, huh). Nothing is 100% confirmed (and, tragically, we're dealing with one of the world's worst purveyors of disinformation for "facts"). A death, quarantine measures and conflicting accounts need real scrutiny, not a passing headline before everyone returns to Trump's _Bedtime for Bonzo_ routine.
Annie Jacobsen--who is THE expert on this--has been sounding the alarm about precisely this danger. Her book, _Biological War: A Scenario_ , explores a hypothetical--but realistic--catastrophe based on a deadly, weaponized pathogen leaked from a Russian lab. That doesn't establish exactly what happened in Irkutsk. But it does explain why the reports are so unsettling: **the possibility of a disastrous biological release was already being examined publicly, before this worker 's death. We cannot claim nobody imagined the danger. Someone wrote an entire book about it**.
It's like Condi Rice claiming nobody could have foreseen 9/11. Ya know, unless you count Algerian hijackers who had planned to crash a plane into the Eiffel Tower:
> On December 24, 1994, four heavily armed members of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), an Algerian Islamist terrorist organization, hijacked **Air France Flight 8969** at Houari Boumediene Airport in Algiers.
> French authorities later discovered that the hijackers' ultimate goal was to fly the Airbus A300 to Paris and **detonate the aircraft over the Eiffel Tower** or the Tour Montparnasse.
Or that _August 6th Presidential Daily Briefing_ titled "Bin Laden Determined to Strike Inside America," that was pretty tough to get. Or the Jihadists we found at U.S. flight schools who only wanted to learn to maneuver flights in the air, not take off or land. Or White House national security hand Richard A. Clarke's "hair on fire" warnings from intel he was seeing. Or how about we just discuss the fact that Tom Clancy had the insight to write a book predicting this scenario. Kinda like Annie Jacobsen.
The questions now are straightforward and must be answered: What killed Shipilova? How widespread was the exposure? Shipilova was sick for around six days, and came into contact with others in the Irkutsk; this bacteria is supposedly ready made to be spread as pneumonic and live on surfaces for periods of time. Does evidence support the official explanation?
The latest Russian account says testing found no pathogens associated with her work (this is where you do the cough from _Animal House ...ahem bullshit)_, and no additional plague infections have been found. These details, and independent verification, **matter**. Axios reports the White House is monitoring the suspected case and related quarantines (great, Orangula is on the case). **A possible biological emergency requires transparent evidence, relentless reporting, and officials who get public trust requires more than telling frightened people to "remain calm."**
